etudes.titre: Risk factors associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE OR PURPOSE: To identify patient characteristics associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use in children.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: Children ≤18 years of age seen at a tertiary care children's hospital between 2009 and 2025 who were prescribed any type of steroid and had a documented intraocular pressure (IOP) measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation. Children with any IOP measurement >21 mmHg recorded prior to or on the day of steroid initiation were excluded.
METHODS: Steroid type, route of administration, and patient characteristics, including comorbidities, were extracted from the electronic medical record. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors independently associated with ocular hypertension after steroid use.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Ocular hypertension among children who underwent IOP measurement after steroid initiation, defined as IOP >21 mmHg measured within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation.
RESULTS: Of 5,687 children included (mean age at steroid initiation 8.8 years; 54.4% male), 1,034 (18.2%) developed ocular hypertension. The most frequently prescribed steroid was fluticasone (20.0%), and the most common route of administration was inhaled/intranasal (24.8%). In multivariable analysis, glaucoma conferred the highest odds of ocular hypertension after steroid use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 6.77; 95% CI, 5.21-8.79), followed by prednisone relative to dexamethasone (aOR, 3.37; 95% CI, 2.30-4.93), juvenile arthritis (aOR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.09-2.24), and uveitis (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.16-1.99). Compared with topical administration, ocular (aOR, 3.57; 95% CI, 2.39-5.33) and intravenous (aOR, 2.63; 95% CI, 1.78-3.89) routes each independently conferred higher odds of ocular hypertension. Age, sex, race, ethnicity, diabetes, and asthma were not independently associated with ocular hypertension.
CONCLUSIONS: Nearly 1 in 5 children with an IOP measurement within 1 to 60 days of steroid initiation developed ocular hypertension. Glaucoma, uveitis, juvenile arthritis, and non-topical routes of administration-particularly ocular and intravenous-were the strongest risk factors, highlighting the importance of ophthalmic monitoring in children receiving glucocorticoid therapy.

etudes.titre: Ocular comorbidities are common in multiple myeloma: results of a large cross-sectional survey.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Both advancing age and multiple myeloma (MM) therapies such as belantamab mafodotin or dexamethasone can be risk factors for ocular complications. We conducted an international online survey of 508 patients with MM; 3% and 2% reported previous craniofacial radiation therapy or belantamab mafodotin, respectively. Common ocular comorbidities included cataracts (59%), dry eyes requiring eyedrops (37%), and blepharitis or styes (24%). Higher typical dexamethasone doses (≥20 milligrams weekly) were associated with cataracts after adjusting for advancing age and time since diagnosis. Compared to lower-dose dexamethasone (0-19 milligrams weekly), high-dose dexamethasone shifted the incidence curve of predicted cataracts approximately 5.4 years earlier. Although 82% of patients reported periodic eye exams (in line with ophthalmologic recommendations for older adults), only 31% had ever received such guidance from their MM teams. In conclusion, ocular issues are common in MM. Corticosteroid-sparing regimens may warrant attention across the age spectrum to reduce the risk of cataracts.

etudes.titre: Long-Term Follow-Up of Nonlethal Raine Syndrome in an Omani Child: A Case Report.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Raine syndrome (RS) is a rare autosomal recessive osteosclerotic skeletal dysplasia caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the FAM20C gene. While the classical phenotype is typically lethal in the neonatal period, an increasing number of nonlethal cases have been recognized. However, long-term clinical follow-up data remain extremely limited.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report the long-term follow-up of a twelve-year-old Omani female with a clinical phenotype consistent with nonlethal RS, born to consanguineous parents. Early manifestations included natal tooth, congenital glaucoma, respiratory distress, and extensive intracranial calcifications. During childhood, she progressively developed hypophosphatemic rickets, severe dental abnormalities, growth impairment, skeletal deformities, osteoporosis, and recurrent airway disease. Whole-exome sequencing identified a homozygous FAM20C variant classified by the reporting laboratory as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS, Class 3). The patient demonstrated clinical and densitometric improvement during bisphosphonate therapy, with reduction in bone pain and improved mobility. A younger sibling with a highly similar clinical phenotype, but who was not genetically tested, exhibited more severe craniofacial and airway involvement, highlighting marked intrafamilial phenotypic variability.
CONCLUSIONS: This report provides one of the longest longitudinal follow-ups of nonlethal RS currently described in the literature. It further expands the phenotypic spectrum of FAM20C-related disease and offers additional insight into long-term skeletal complications and therapeutic response. Early recognition and multidisciplinary long-term follow-up are essential to optimize outcomes in affected individuals.

etudes.titre: Azo-based prodrugs therapeutic systems: From microbial azoreducases and tumor reductases activation to medicinal chemistry perspectives.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: National Natural Science Foundation of China

etudes.resume: Azo-based hypoxia-responsive prodrugs and delivery systems have emerged as a promising strategy for targeted therapy in diseases characterized by hypoxic microenvironments, particularly solid tumors. In this article, we examine and review the recent advances in the design strategy, activation mechanisms, and biomedical applications of azo-based prodrugs. These systems operate on a mechanistic principle whereby azo bonds (-NN-) undergo selective reduction by gut bacterial azoreductases and reductases present in the hypoxic microenvironment, which enables spatially selective drug release in hypoxic regions for targeted therapy. We further discuss how azo-based prodrugs have been integrated with complementary therapeutic modalities, including photodynamic therapy, photothermal therapy, sonodynamic or ultrasound-triggered therapy, and enzyme-catalyzed oxygen-depletion strategies. Particular attention is given to the incorporation of azo bonds into multifunctional carriers, including nanoparticles and host-guest systems, as well as to their use in hypoxia-responsive fluorescent and theranostic probes. Beyond tumor-targeted therapy, azo-based approaches have also shown potential in other hypoxia-related diseases, including glaucoma, stroke, and pulmonary fibrosis. Finally, we delineate the key challenges and future opportunities for the clinical translation of azo-based hypoxia-activated prodrugs.

etudes.titre: Development of machine learning models to predict chemical-induced ocular irritation.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « machine learning »

labos.nom: U S Army Medical Research and Development Command
US Army Medical Research and Development Command

etudes.resume: Chemical-induced ocular irritation can lead to acute tissue damage and chronic eye conditions, such as glaucoma or vision loss; therefore, assessing the ocular irritation potential of chemicals is important to protect human health. However, because the amount of available human data is limited, we must often extrapolate animal data for human risk assessment, which can be imprecise and resource-intensive, as well as pose ethical concerns. New approach methodologies offer an opportunity to streamline chemical risk assessment and reduce the need for animal testing. In this study, we modified and enhanced our previously published computational workflow to build and systematically compare 49 classification models, spanning seven molecular representations and nine machine learning algorithms, for predicting chemical-induced ocular irritation. We applied Butina clustering to create structurally distinct training and test sets, and we evaluated all the models using a five-fold cross-validation, repeated five times, and statistical testing. The best model, i.e., the tabular prior-data fitted network (TabPFN) model trained with Mordred descriptors, achieved an accuracy of 0.76 and a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.52, while the evaluation on the held-out test set yielded an accuracy of 0.70 and an MCC of 0.40, indicating a moderate decline in predictive performance but supporting the model's ability to generalize to previously unseen compounds. The classification models we developed here offer a new approach methodology to efficiently and cost-effectively assess the ocular irritation potential of chemicals.

etudes.titre: Integrating quantitative biometrics and automated risk stratification for ophthalmic surgical triage.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgical »
etudes.resume: Ophthalmology generates extensive quantitative data from ocular biometry and imaging, yet these device-derived measurements are often separated from medical, social, and utilization data in the electronic health record (EHR). No validated ophthalmic tool currently integrates these streams for real-time, patient-specific perioperative decision support. This mini-review examines how automated EHR-based risk stratification and quantitative ocular biometrics could support perioperative decision-making. Across surgical specialties, cancellation models using demographic, comorbidity, socioeconomic, and appointment-related variables have achieved development areas under the curve (AUC) of 0.75-0.92 with a validation range of 0.70-0.74. When the bundle is paired with targeted care pathways, reduced same-day cancellations have been observed, although bundle designs prevent quantifying the independent contribution of the model. In cataract surgery, Epic's Health Composite Score independently predicts same-day cancellation but provides only limited discrimination, and does not predict operative or postoperative outcomes, which remain more closely associated with ocular complexity and surgeon-related factors. Cataract and glaucoma literature identifies additional candidate predictors of technical complexity, surgical outcomes, and access, including pupil and lens characteristics, axial length, anterior chamber anatomy, prior ocular surgery, angle dimensions, conjunctival imaging, frailty, and social vulnerability. We propose an EHR-integrated framework with endpoint- and procedure-specific models for surgical readiness, technical complexity, and adverse outcomes. Each output should be linked to a defined response, such as patient navigation, anesthesia review, case assignment, operative setting, equipment planning, or intensified postoperative follow-up. Prospective multicenter development should assess whether model-guided interventions improve access, efficiency, and outcomes.

etudes.titre: From Algorithm to Care: AI-Assisted Glaucoma Screening in Real-World Settings.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « AI »; mot du titre : « AI-Assisted »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma screening is increasingly being discussed in the context of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly as imaging technologies become more accessible outside specialist clinics. The question, however, is not simply whether AI can identify a suspicious optic nerve head, but whether it can contribute to a screening pathway that works in real-world clinical settings. Fundus image-based AI has shown promising performance and is now being explored in community and primary eye care. The clinical value of these advances, however, depends on how effectively AI-assisted screening integrates into routine care pathways. Media opacity and poor-quality images can limit assessment, indiscriminate screening can generate unnecessary referrals, and many patients who are identified as requiring further evaluation may not complete the referral pathway. In glaucoma, the value of AI-assisted screening depends on its ability to facilitate appropriate clinical assessment and subsequent care for those identified as being at risk. AI is therefore best considered one part of a screening strategy rather than a replacement for clinical assessment. Risk-based selection, early recognition of ungradable images, and appropriate management of visually significant cataracts or other media opacity may make screening more efficient. Portable or tablet-based visual field testing could add functional assessment at the primary-care level, although its role remains to be established. The next phase of AI-based glaucoma screening should therefore focus less on improving performance metrics in isolation and more on understanding where the technology fits within existing eye-care services. The ultimate measure of success is not the number of suspicious optic nerve heads an algorithm identifies, but whether people with previously undetected glaucoma reach timely diagnosis, treatment, and ongoing care.

etudes.titre: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion With Signs of Ocular Hypoperfusion After Parent Artery Occlusion for a Traumatic Carotid-Cavernous Fistula: A Case Report.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: A carotid-cavernous fistula (CCF) can cause a wide range of ocular complications, including venous stasis retinopathy, secondary glaucoma, and central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO). Retinal complications have been reported after endovascular closure of the shunt, but there are few reports describing the ophthalmic course of an eye in which the shunt persisted and in which parent artery occlusion of the internal carotid artery was required. A 63-year-old man was diagnosed with a traumatic right internal carotid artery CCF after a road traffic injury and underwent endovascular treatment on the second and third days after the injury. Because both the transvenous and the transarterial approaches were unsuccessful, parent artery occlusion of the right internal carotid artery was performed. According to the report from the referring institution, occlusion of the shunt was incomplete, and shunt flow into the right superior ophthalmic vein persisted. Angiography approximately six months after the injury confirmed the residual shunt, and no further endovascular treatment was considered feasible. Two months later, the patient noticed decreased vision in the right eye, presented to a local ophthalmologist, and was referred to our department. At presentation, best-corrected visual acuity was 0.2 (logMAR 0.70) in the right eye, and the intraocular pressure (IOP) was 14 mmHg. The right eye showed dilated episcleral vessels, dilated retinal veins, attenuated retinal arteries, retinal hemorrhages extending from the posterior pole to the periphery, and marked macular edema, but venous tortuosity was not prominent. The pupillary light reflex was reduced, and pharmacologic mydriasis was poor, without posterior synechiae or iris atrophy. Spontaneous pulsation of the central retinal artery was present in the affected eye and was augmented by gentle digital pressure, whereas no pulsation was seen in the fellow eye. On widefield fluorescein angiography, dye first entered the central retinal artery 20.1 seconds after the start of injection and complete arterial filling was reached at 25 seconds; numerous microaneurysms were seen from the posterior pole to the mid-periphery, with widespread vascular leakage and reduced perfusion of the retinal capillary network. The fellow eye showed only a few microaneurysms and scattered hard exudates, consistent with mild nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy. The patient had type 2 diabetes mellitus, untreated for approximately 10 years and restarted after the current injury, and hypertension. An intravitreal injection of an aflibercept biosimilar 2 mg was given on the day of presentation, followed by panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) delivered in four sessions for a total of 1,580 burns. Twenty-five days after the injection, the macular edema had clearly decreased but had not completely resolved, and it had recurred by day 67. Throughout the course, the IOP remained consistently lower in the affected eye than in the fellow eye. No iris or angle neovascularization was observed. In this eye, findings of CRVO coexisted with findings suggesting reduced ocular perfusion pressure. Even in a patient with systemic risk factors, local factors should be considered when the findings are confined to, or markedly more severe in, one eye. When no further treatment of the causative lesion is possible, management of the ocular complications is limited to ophthalmic measures, and their effects and limitations must be evaluated separately.

etudes.titre: Assessing Visual Field Defects in Glaucoma Using the Perceptive Scotoma Finder.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Visual Field »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of the Perceptive Scotoma Finder, a dynamic touchscreen-based tool, for detecting glaucomatous visual field defects and examining its structure-function associations.
METHODS: From the initial cohort of 143 eyes (86 participants), one eye per participant was included to avoid inter-eye correlation bias, comprising 58 glaucomatous eyes and 28 control eyes. All participants underwent monocular testing with a 30 Hz flickering dot stimulus mapped onto the Humphrey Visual Field 24-2 grid. Sectoral detection scores were compared with Humphrey Visual Field indices and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness. Group differences were analyzed with Mann-Whitney U tests, correlations with Spearman's rho, and diagnostic accuracy with receiver operating characteristic analysis. Test-retest reliability of the mean sector score was assessed in a subset of 26 eyes, including 18 glaucoma patients and 8 control subjects, using a two-way random-effects model for absolute agreement.
RESULTS: Perceptive Scotoma Finder detection proportions were markedly higher in glaucoma than in controls across all Garway-Heath sectors (e.g., IN: 85.7% vs 1.9%; all p < 0.001). Detection scores showed correlations with mean deviation (ρ = 0.29 to 0.50) and pattern standard deviation (ρ = 0.36 to 0.69; all p < 0.001), and with RNFL thickness in all sectors except the temporal sector (p = 0.252). Sensitivity ranged from 0.68 to 0.91 and specificity from 0.83 to 0.90 across sectors. Test-retest reliability, based on 26 eyes, was 0.76 (95% confidence interval 0.72-0.89) by ICC, and Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of 0.00 with 95% limits of agreement from -0.24 to 0.24. Overall discriminative performance produced an area under the curve of 0.79 (95% Confidence interval 0.76-0.83).
CONCLUSIONS: The Perceptive Scotoma Finder demonstrated reproducible, sector-specific detection of established glaucomatous visual field defects and showed moderate agreement with conventional visual field and RNFL measures. These findings support its feasibility and potential as a rapid, low-cost adjunctive tool for glaucoma assessment; however, further evaluation in early glaucoma and screening populations is required.

etudes.titre: Worksite Vision Screening for Farmworkers: A California Bay Area Pilot Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Screening »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Farmworkers face high risk of ocular disease, yet substantial barriers to vision care. We conducted a pilot implementation of a worksite vision screening at a commercial farm, characterizing participant demographics, ocular pathology, vision-related quality of life, and barriers to care.
METHODS: A one-time vision screening was conducted at a farm in the California Bay Area. Participants completed a demographic intake, the Vision Quality of Life (VisQoL) Index, and a survey on self-reported barriers to care. All received an eye exam, including visual acuity, intraocular pressure, slit lamp, and dilated fundus evaluation. Glasses were distributed on-site. Patients with pathology requiring follow-up were referred to in-network providers.
RESULTS: Eighty-five farmworkers were screened (mean age 47.1 years; 71.8% male). Best presenting visual acuity was 20/40 or worse in 20.0% of participants. The most common diagnoses were refractive error (81.2%, including presbyopia and astigmatism), cataracts (22.4%), dry eye/meibomian gland dysfunction (20.0%), and glaucoma suspect (16.5%). Nineteen participants (22.4%) were referred for further care. Of ten participants with self-reported diabetes, three had diabetic retinopathy. The most common barriers were cost (20.0%), competing work or caregiving obligations (15.3%), and appointment difficulty (11.8%).
CONCLUSION: This worksite screening reached over one-third of the workforce in a single day, provided same-day refractive correction to 62.4% of participants, and identified previously undetected ocular pathology. It may represent a scalable approach for delivering preventive eye care to farmworker communities with limited access to clinic-based services, although feasibility and linkage to follow-up care were not assessed.

etudes.titre: Risks of long-term ophthalmic complications in preterm and ROP: a 14-year population-based study in Taiwan.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the 14-year (2004-2017) epidemiology and newborn demographic risk factors for preterm- and retinopathy of prematurity (ROP)-associated ophthalmic complications using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD).
DESIGN: Retrospective Cohort Study.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 1,784,677 infants were recorded from the maternal and children database of the NHIRD.
METHODS: Data were retrieved from the NHIRD, and patients were stratified into full-term, preterm without ROP, and ROP groups. Six ophthalmic complications were recorded and compared, including myopia, amblyopia, glaucoma, strabismus, cataracts, and retinal detachment. The average follow-up time for the recorded ophthalmic complications was between 6.5 to 7.2 person-years. The hazard ratios (HRs) for patients with ROP were calculated for each complication, using full-term infants as the reference group.
RESULTS: A total of 1,784,677 infants born between 2004 and 2017 were enrolled, and 0.56% were diagnosed with ROP. ROP was identified as a risk factor for myopia, amblyopia, strabismus, cataracts, and retinal detachment (all p<0.05). ROP-associated glaucoma, cataracts, and retinal detachment showed extremely early onset within the first 2 years of life, identifying them as high-risk complications among patients with ROP. Multivariate analysis showed a trend of lower birth weight being associated with a higher risk of developing ROP-associated complications of myopia, amblyopia, glaucoma, and strabismus.
CONCLUSION: Prematurity, especially in the presence of ROP, carries a higher risk of ophthalmic complications, which often present early in the first decade of life. Low BW among patients with ROP is also associated with elevated risks of ophthalmic complications.

etudes.titre: Visual and clinical outcomes of different IOL implantation strategies following posterior capsule rupture.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To compare visual outcomes and postoperative complication rates associated with different intraocular lens (IOL) implantation strategies following posterior capsule rupture (PCR) with vitreous loss during cataract surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included eyes that underwent cataract surgery complicated by PCR and anterior vitrectomy between 2012 and 2021 at a tertiary referral center. Eyes were grouped according to IOL implantation strategy: three-piece sulcus IOL (BAL-65), anterior chamber IOL (AC-IOL), or iris-fixated IOL (ARTISAN). Primary outcome was change in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) from preoperative baseline to 6 months postoperatively, after exclusion of eyes with preoperative visual-limiting pathology. Secondary outcomes included rates of postoperative complications, specifically glaucoma, corneal endothelial insufficiency, cystoid macular edema, retinal detachment, and complications leading to poor visual outcome.
RESULTS: A total of 249 eyes were included (102 AC-IOL, 54 ARTISAN, 93 BAL-65). After exclusion of eyes with preoperative visual-limiting conditions, three-piece sulcus IOL implantation was associated with significantly greater visual improvement compared with both AC-IOL and Iris-fixated IOL implantation (mean ΔBCVA 1.06 vs. 0.47 and 0.54 LogMAR, respectively; p < 0.01). No significant difference in visual improvement was observed between AC-IOL and Iris-fixated IOL groups. Postoperative complications occurred more frequently in the AC-IOL group, particularly secondary glaucoma (6.9% vs. 1.9% and 1.0% in Iris-fixated IOL and sulcus IOL groups, respectively). Complications leading to poor visual outcome were significantly more common in AC-IOL compared with sulcus IOL (22.7% vs. 9.8%, p = 0.021).
CONCLUSIONS: In eyes with PCR and vitreous loss, three-piece sulcus IOL implantation was associated with greater visual improvement and fewer vision-threatening complications than AC-IOL implantation, supporting sulcus placement when adequate capsular support is present.

etudes.titre: Long-term outcomes of a novel non-haptic exposure technique for sutureless, glueless intrascleral fixation of a 3-piece intraocular lens: a single surgeon series of 553 eyes.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the long-term outcomes of a novel non-haptic exposure technique for sutureless, glueless intrascleral fixation of a 3-piece intraocular lens (IOL) in eyes with inadequate capsular support.
SUBJECTS/METHODS: This study included 553 eyes of 524 consecutive patients who underwent the non-haptic exposure technique for sutureless, glueless intrascleral fixation of a 3-piece IOL between June 2017 and June 2025. Eyes with active inflammation, uncontrolled glaucoma, severe corneal opacity, or follow up of less than 6 months were excluded. The primary outcome was final best corrected visual acuity (BCVA). Secondary outcomes included uncorrected visual acuity (UCVA) and postoperative complications. Subgroup analysis compared surgical aphakia following cataract surgery (Group A) with other secondary aetiologies (Group B).
RESULTS: Mean BCVA improved from 0.60 to 0.20 logMAR (p = 0.002). Mean UCVA improved from 1.47 (SD 0.64) to 0.35 (SD 0.36) logMAR (p < 0.001), with 77% of eyes achieving a final visual acuity of 0.48 logMAR or better. Late postoperative complications included cystoid macular oedema (6.7%), retinal detachment (2.9%), and IOL subluxation (2.2%). Retinal detachment occurred more frequently in Group B than in Group A (p = 0.039). No eye developed haptic extrusion, scleral erosion, or acute endophthalmitis during follow up.
CONCLUSIONS: The non-haptic exposure technique for sutureless, glueless intrascleral fixation of a 3-piece IOL provided favourable long-term visual outcomes with a low incidence of postoperative complications in eyes with inadequate capsular support. The absence of haptic extrusion and scleral erosion throughout follow up supports the long-term stability of this technique.

etudes.titre: Home and Workplace Secondhand Smoke and Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer Thinning in Never-Smokers: A Nationwide Population-Based Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To examine the association of home and workplace secondhand smoke (SHS) exposure with circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (cpRNFL) thickness, macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) thickness, and glaucoma among lifetime never-smokers.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional, nationwide population-based study.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 4,276 lifetime never-smokers (354 with SHS exposure and 3,922 without SHS exposure) from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2019-2021.
METHODS: Self-reported SHS exposure at home or in the workplace was the primary exposure. cpRNFL and macular GCIPL thicknesses were measured using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography, and glaucoma was centrally adjudicated according to the International Society of Geographical and Epidemiological Ophthalmology criteria. Survey-weighted linear and logistic regression analyses were performed to investigate the associations of SHS exposure with cpRNFL thickness, macular GCIPL thickness, and glaucoma. Trends across the number of exposure settings were also evaluated.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: cpRNFL thickness, macular GCIPL thickness, and glaucoma.
RESULTS: Compared with unexposed never-smokers, SHS-exposed participants were younger (47.0±13.1 vs. 49.0±14.0 years, standardized mean difference [SMD]=-0.144), had a greater intraocular pressure (15.1±2.3 vs. 14.9±2.3 mmHg, SMD=0.106), deeper anterior chamber (2.79±0.32 vs. 2.74±0.32 mm, SMD=0.155), and a thinner global cpRNFL (93.0±9.9 vs. 94.4±9.9 µm, SMD=-0.145), whereas axial length, macular GCIPL thickness, and glaucoma prevalence (4.4% vs. 3.4%, SMD=0.054) did not differ. After full adjustment, SHS exposure was associated with thinner global cpRNFL (β=-1.826, 95% confidence interval [CI]=-3.082 to -0.570, P=0.004), with a significant trend across the number of exposure settings (P for trend=0.003). In sectoral analyses, thinner cpRNFL was observed in the inferior (β=-3.003, P=0.006) and temporal (β=-1.429, P=0.012) sectors, which remained significant after Bonferroni correction. Exposed never-smokers had higher odds of belonging to the thinnest cpRNFL quartile (odds ratio=1.485, 95% CI=1.081 to 2.039, P=0.015). Average macular GCIPL thickness (P=0.617) and glaucoma (P=0.170) were not significantly associated with SHS exposure.
CONCLUSIONS: SHS exposure was associated with cpRNFL thinning in lifetime never-smokers, but not with macular GCIPL thickness or glaucoma. These findings suggest a subclinical structural vulnerability of the cpRNFL to SHS exposure and underscore the public health imperative of reducing SHS exposure to protect ocular neuroaxonal health in never-smokers.

etudes.titre: MoViT-Eye model: A robust and explainable AI-driven approach for automated multi-class ocular disease diagnosis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « AI »; mot du titre : « diagnosis »
etudes.resume: Ocular diseases, including Diabetic Retinopathy (DR), Glaucoma, Pterygium, and Retinal Detachment, require early detection to prevent irreversible blindness. However, manual screening is labor-intensive, and standard deep learning models often fail to capture the complex global spatial relationships necessary for multipathology grading. To address these limitations, we propose a MobileNetV2-Transformer Hybrid (MoViT-Eye) architecture for the automated 5-class classification of fundus images. This framework integrates the efficient local spatial feature extraction of MobileNetV2 with the long-range dependency modeling of Transformers. The study uses 4,906 cleaned images and applies LIME, Grad-CAM++, and Saliency Maps to identify image regions that influence each prediction. These methods generate heatmaps that highlight important clinical features, including microaneurysms and optic disc abnormalities, and support transparent clinical decision-making. The proposed model significantly outperforms existing architectures, achieving an accuracy of 90.36%, a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.8643, a Cohen's Kappa of 0.8640, and a specificity of 97.29%. The model achieved an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 98.60% for identifying DR and Retinal Detachment. By combining hybrid feature learning with multi-layered interpretability, this model provides a robust and transparent tool for automated clinical ophthalmic screening.

etudes.titre: Ocular Complications Related to Iris-Fixated Phakic Intraocular Lens Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
TOPIC: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the cumulative prevalence of ocular complications following implantation of Artisan®/Verisyse® iris-fixated phakic intraocular lenses in adult patients undergoing refractive surgery. Outcomes included postoperative ocular complications and longitudinal loss of endothelial cell density (ECD).
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Phakic intraocular lenses are widely used to correct moderate-to-high refractive errors. Available evidence on complication rates is heterogeneous and often limited to narrative reports, hindering accurate risk counseling and long-term clinical decision-making.
METHODS: This study was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251150677). Eligible studies included ≥10 eyes implanted with Artisan®/Verisyse® lenses reporting postoperative complications. Risk of bias was assessed using design-specific tools. Proportion meta-analyses were performed with subgroup analyses comparing real-world evidence studies versus clinical trials. ECD loss was analyzed from three months to 10 years post-implantation. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.
RESULTS: Fifty-five studies were included. Iris atrophy was the most common complication (20.3%, 95% CI: 5.7-52.1). Other complications included pupil ovalization (7.6%, 95% CI: 4.8-12.5), progressive reduction in visual acuity (7.6%, 95% CI: 5.8-9.5), position-related complications (including rotation, dislocation, subluxation, and luxation) (6.7%, 95% CI: 1.9-33.4), uveitis (6.2%, 95% CI: 4.3-9.1), and halos (5.3%, 95% CI: 3.2-7.9). Ocular hypertension (4.7%, 95% CI: 2.4-7.9), cataract (2.8%, 95% CI: 1.6-3.5), corneal decompensation (2.6%, 95% CI: 1.8-6.5), and retinal detachment (1.1%, 95% CI: 0.7-1.3) occurred less frequently. Subgroup analyses showed higher rates of corneal decompensation in real-world studies (4.2% vs. 1.3%; p = 0.04) and traumatic position-related complications (5.0% vs. 0.8%; p = 0.02), whereas ocular hypertension was more frequent in clinical trials (14.1% vs. 2.3%; p < 0.01). ECD loss increased from 5.3% at 3 months to 15.8% at 10 years. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate, with substantial heterogeneity across outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Despite overall acceptable safety, Artisan®/Verisyse® implantation is associated with measurable ocular complications and progressive ECD loss.
etudes.revue: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

etudes.titre: Integrated metabolomics and transcriptomics reveal retinal alterations in a mouse model of chronic restraint stress protocol-induced anxiety-like behavior.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « mouse »; mot du titre : « transcriptomics »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Psychological stress is a potential risk factor for glaucoma, but the association and underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether a chronic restraint stress (CRS) protocol, which includes repeated fasting/water deprivation, is associated with glaucoma-like retinal damage in mice and explored the involved pathways.
METHODS: Adult male mice underwent 4 h daily restraint for 10 days. Anxiety-like behaviors were assessed by open field test (OFT) and elevated plus maze (EPM). Intraocular pressure (IOP) was measured at baseline, day 7, and day 14. Retinal ganglion cell (RGC) survival was quantified by RBPMS immunofluorescence. RNA-seq and untargeted metabolomics (UHPLC-MS/MS) were performed on retinas, followed by integrated analysis, qPCR validation, and a targeted query of the GWAS Catalog for glaucoma-associated SNPs.
RESULTS: CRS mice showed anxiety-like behaviors, progressive IOP elevation, and reduced RGC numbers. Transcriptomics identified 216 candidate genes with nominal differential expression, with altered oxidoreductase activity and iron ion binding. Metabolomics detected 255 differential metabolites, mainly fatty acids, glycerophospholipids, and amino acids, with nominal enrichment of the thermogenesis pathway. qPCR confirmed upregulation of Cyp2f2, Cyp4f15, Fmo2, S100a9, and Aif1. Integrated analysis identified Fmo2 and Serpine1 as candidate genes that may contribute to the link between the CRS protocol and glaucoma pathogenesis; Serpine1 had records of glaucoma-risk SNPs in the GWAS Catalog.
CONCLUSION: The CRS protocol is associated with glaucoma-like retinal degeneration, characterized by IOP elevation, RGC loss, and dysregulation of metabolic, oxidative stress, and inflammatory pathways. Fmo2 and Serpine1 are candidate genes that may link the CRS protocol to glaucoma pathogenesis; however, functional validation is required to establish causality.

etudes.titre: Astaxanthin attenuates H2O2-induced oxidative injury in R28 retinal precursor cells via the Keap1-Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « pathway »
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the protective effects of astaxanthin (AST) against H2O2-induced oxidative injury in R28 retinal precursor cells using network pharmacology and in vitro experiments, and to evaluate the involvement of the Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1)-nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) antioxidant pathway.
METHODS: Network pharmacology was used to identify shared targets of AST and glaucoma, construct a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network, and perform Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses and molecular docking. An oxidative stress model was established in rat R28 retinal precursor cells using hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). Cells were assigned to control, H2O2, AST + H2O2, AST + H2O2 + ML385, ML385-alone, and H2O2 + ML385 groups; an AST-alone group was included in selected experiments. Cell viability, reactive oxygen species (ROS), superoxide dismutase (SOD), malondialdehyde (MDA), 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG), protein carbonyls, mitochondrial membrane potential, Nrf2 nuclear translocation, inflammation-related genes and proteins, apoptosis-related proteins, and expression of Keap1-Nrf2/HO-1/NQO1 pathway molecules were assessed. Reverse validation was performed using the Nrf2 inhibitor ML385.
RESULTS: Network pharmacology indicated that the mechanisms by which AST may act in glaucoma involve oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. H2O2 treatment reduced R28 cell viability, increased ROS, MDA, 8-OHdG, and protein carbonyl levels, decreased SOD activity, and induced inflammation, loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, and an imbalance in apoptosis-related proteins. AST treatment reversed these changes, downregulated Keap1, upregulated Nrf2, HO-1, and NQO1, and promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation. ML385 partially attenuated the antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic effects of AST.
CONCLUSION: AST may alleviate H2O2-induced oxidative injury, inflammation, and apoptosis in R28 cells by activating the Keap1-Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway. These findings provide experimental evidence for the potential protective role of AST in glaucoma-related oxidative stress, although its use as an adjunctive neuroprotective strategy for glaucoma requires further validation in animal models that more closely recapitulate the clinical pathology.

etudes.titre: Laser-Induced Trabecular Damage Converts Segmentally Uncorrelated to Coupled Aqueous Humor Outflow Pathways in Non-Human Primates.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Laser »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Trabecular and uveoscleral outflow are segmental and uncorrelated in healthy eyes. This study investigated whether trabecular meshwork (TM) injury alters segmental flow and induces coupling between pathways in a laser-induced ocular hypertensive primate model.
METHODS: Five female cynomolgus macaques underwent unilateral ∼270° TM laser photocoagulation; contralateral non-laser-treated eyes served as normotensive controls. Intraocular pressure (IOP) was monitored. Fluorescent tracers were injected intracamerally and diffused for 45 minutes before fixation. Twelve radial segments per eye were imaged using confocal microscopy. Tracer intensity, ciliary stromal thickness, TM-ciliary muscle (CM) bridge prevalence, and communication channels linking supraciliary space to trabecular pathway were quantified. Histology validated these findings.
RESULTS: Laser treatment significantly elevated IOP, which was negatively correlated with tracer intensity in the trabecular pathway and combined tracer intensity across both pathways. Segmental outflow was observed in both pathways in all eyes. In laser-treated eyes, trabecular outflow was largely confined to the non-lasered TM. The two pathways were uncorrelated in control eyes but positively correlated in laser-treated eyes. TM-CM bridge prevalence decreased after laser treatment and was negatively correlated with IOP. Communication channels showed similar prevalence between groups; however, tracer intensities in the two pathways were positively correlated at locations containing these channels.
CONCLUSIONS: TM photocoagulation impairs trabecular outflow and induces anterior segment remodeling, thereby altering segmental flow and functional coupling between pathways. Loss of the TM-CM bridge and recruitment of preexisting communication channels may contribute to this interaction, suggesting that aqueous outflow pathways behave as an interconnected system following trabecular injury.

etudes.titre: The gut-eye axis in clinical ophthalmology: current evidence and translational perspectives.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « axis »

labos.nom: Beijing Natural Science Foundation-Haidian Original Innovation Joint Fund
National High Level Hospital Clinical Research Funding and Cancer Hospital Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Cooperative Fund

etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: The gut-eye axis has emerged as a potential link between gut microbiota dysbiosis and ocular inflammation, neurovascular injury, and immune-mediated diseases. However, the clinical relevance and translational readiness of microbiome-related findings remain uncertain. This review evaluates current clinical evidence and explores opportunities for integrating gut-eye axis research into ophthalmic practice.
METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov through September 28, 2026. A total of 92 records were included, encompassing observational studies, longitudinal cohorts, clinical interventions, Mendelian randomization studies, systematic reviews, and relevant methodological literature. Evidence was descriptively mapped according to study design, clinical relevance, consistency, reproducibility, and methodological limitations.
RESULTS: Human evidence was relatively more developed for dry eye disease, particularly Sjögren's syndrome-associated dry eye, diabetic retinopathy, age-related macular degeneration/geographic atrophy, neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, and Graves orbitopathy. Randomized trials of microbiome-related interventions in dry eye disease reported heterogeneous outcomes. Longitudinal studies in diabetic retinopathy identified candidate microbial and metabolic predictors, while multicenter observations supported microbiome associations with Graves orbitopathy. Evidence for uveitis varied across disease subtypes, whereas findings for glaucoma and other emerging ocular conditions remained largely exploratory. Major limitations included small sample sizes, treatment-relatedcon founding, methodological heterogeneity, and insufficient external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: The gut-eye axis provides a promising framework for investigating ocular disease mechanisms and potential biomarkers, but current evidence does not support routine microbiome testing or microbiome-targeted treatment in ophthalmology. Clinical translation requires standardized methodologies, independent longitudinal validation, integration with established ophthalmic indicators, and adequately powered randomized controlled trials demonstrating incremental clinical benefit.

etudes.titre: Management of Ahmed Glaucoma Valve Plate Exposure by Plate Removal and Tube Retention: A Case Report.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Valve »; mot du titre : « Tube »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Ahmed glaucoma valve (AGV) implantation is an established option for refractory glaucoma, including neovascular glaucoma (NVG). Exposure of glaucoma drainage device hardware is a serious complication because it increases the risk of infection and may require surgical repair or explantation.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 66-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension, and NVG secondary to diabetic retinopathy developed AGV plate exposure in the right eye two months after implantation. The exposed plate was removed while the tube was retained. The distal open end of the retained tube was positioned subconjunctivally approximately 8 mm posterior to the limbus beneath conjunctival/Tenon tissue. The tube was fixed to the sclera with 10-0 nylon, temporarily ligated with 7-0 Vicryl, and three fenestrations were created proximal to the ligature. Two weeks later, conjunctival wound dehiscence with tube exposure occurred and was repaired with an approximately 4 × 2 mm preserved scleral patch graft. At eight months after the final repair, the eye was quiet, the tube remained covered, and IOP was 14 mmHg while the patient was using dorzolamide-timolol. Tube function was not objectively confirmed.
CONCLUSION: This case suggests that removal of an exposed Ahmed glaucoma valve (AGV) plate with retention of the tube may preserve a potential aqueous drainage pathway. However, subsequent conjunctival wound dehiscence and tube exposure required repair with a preserved scleral patch graft, highlighting the importance of adequate tube coverage, particularly in eyes with compromised conjunctiva. Following repair, tube coverage remained intact and intraocular pressure remained stable during eight months of follow-up, although the independent contribution of the retained tube to IOP control could not be confirmed. Longer follow-up and additional cases are needed to establish the efficacy and safety of this individualized approach.

etudes.titre: Tracking Retinal Ganglion Cell Soma Loss in Glaucoma Reveals Progression Over Months and Years.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Retinal Ganglion Cell »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: Adaptive optics optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) has the potential to transform how glaucoma progression is assessed by directly measuring loss of ganglion cells over time. Here, we used AO-OCT to measure ganglion cell layer (GCL) soma loss in glaucoma subjects over time intervals as short as 3 months.
METHODS: We recruited six glaucoma subjects with moderate-to-severe primary open-angle, low-tension, or pigmentary glaucoma (63.2 ± 3.4 years, mean ± SD) and two age-similar controls. AO-OCT volumes traversing arcuate defects were acquired at both multi-year (2-8 years, 3 subjects) and sub-year (3-12 months, all subjects) intervals. GCL soma count and layer thickness were measured in four to six subregions per subject to determine annualized loss rate (%/yr) across the defect. Clinical OCT thickness measurements were also acquired.
RESULTS: Annualized GCL soma loss rates in the 3 multi-year subjects were -1.8, -10.3, and -5.4%/yr, exceeding aging rates in controls by approximately 5 to 28 times. Loss was detectable in all subjects at 3- to 6-month intervals (-0.35 to -7.8%/yr). Soma density loss and GCL thinning rates were weakly correlated when the follow-up interval was under 1 year (glaucomatous: r = 0.32; healthy: r = 0.34). Variation in loss rate across the arcuate defect was significant over sub-year intervals, with the highest rates near the defect edge. Clinical OCT measurements did not exceed progression thresholds in any subject over sub-year intervals.
CONCLUSIONS: AO-OCT can detect individual glaucomatous GCL soma loss over intervals as short as 3 months, at rates clearly distinguishable from age-related decline. Glaucomatous rates were subclinical by OCT and peaked within the arcuate defect.

etudes.titre: Thermal Skin Burns Following Infrared Vein Finder Application in Pediatric Patients: A Report of 2 Cases and Protocol Revision.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral venous cannulation remains a cornerstone of pediatric anesthesia practice. Infrared vein finder devices have gained popularity as aids to improve venous visualization in children with difficult access. However, the thermal hazards associated with certain device types, particularly pocket flashlight-based models, remain underappreciated among clinical staff.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report 2 pediatric patients who sustained grade 2 thermal burns at peripheral venous access sites following the use of a pocket flashlight-based infrared vein finder during ophthalmic surgical procedures. The first patient, an 8-month-old girl born at term with appropriate developmental milestones undergoing congenital cataract surgery, developed a ruptured blister on her left elbow after 45 minutes of intermittent device application across multiple sites. The second patient, a 1-year-old boy, born preterm at 32 weeks gestation (birth weight of 1.9 kg) with delayed milestones scheduled for examination under anesthesia for congenital glaucoma, developed thermal blisters on his right palm. Retrospective review of operating room closed-circuit television footage confirmed the device had been in continuous contact with the right palm for approximately 5 minutes during the initial cannulation attempt. Notably, the contralateral palm remained unaffected, where device contact lasted only 2 minutes. Both injuries occurred in the absence of any underlying dermatological conditions.
CONCLUSION: These cases highlight a patient safety concern regarding pocket flashlight-based vein finders. We advocate for institutional protocol revisions including mandatory time limits for device application, preoperative skin assessments, and preferential use of LED-based devices with established safety profiles. Awareness of device-specific thermal risks is essential to prevent iatrogenic harm.

etudes.titre: Ocular hyperemia with netarsudil/latanoprost fixed combination in glaucoma: an exploratory association analysis of tolerability outcomes by prior topical therapy and baseline ocular hyperemia.
etudes.raison_rubrique: étiquette : produit suivi étudié (rôle suggéré, à vérifier)
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: This post hoc analysis of MERCURY-3 evaluates factors associated with baseline ocular hyperemia and tolerability outcomes with netarsudil/latanoprost fixed combination (NET/LAT).
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: MERCURY-3 was a prospective, randomized, double-masked, multicenter, Phase 3, European trial. Adults with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension inadequately controlled on topical therapy were randomized to once-daily NET/LAT (n = 218) or bimatoprost/timolol fixed combination (BIM/TIM; n = 212) for 6 months. Patients were stratified by baseline ocular hyperemia status (none vs any grade) and associations with prior treatment, adverse events (AEs), and hyperemia evolution evaluated.
RESULTS: In the NET/LAT arm, prior combination therapy was associated with a greater prevalence of baseline ocular hyperemia than prior monotherapy (distribution: p = 0.003). Patients with baseline hyperemia experienced higher rates of AEs (85% vs 63%), ocular treatment-related AEs (74% vs 39%), and conjunctival hyperemia (45% vs 26%) during treatment. Ocular hyperemia remained predominantly mild throughout follow-up, with a more stable severity trajectory linked to prior monotherapy compared with prior combination therapy. No comparable associations were observed with BIM/TIM.
CONCLUSIONS: Prior treatment complexity and baseline ocular hyperemia status are associated with tolerability outcomes during NET/LAT therapy. These exploratory findings suggest that earlier step-up after monotherapy could be associated with more favorable tolerability.

etudes.titre: Dietary Lutein, Vegetable and Nut Intake, and Open-Angle Glaucoma: The Maastricht Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique

labos.nom: Care and Public Health Research Institute
NUTRIM School of Nutrition and Translational Research in Metabolism

etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether total dietary lutein intake, intake of lutein derived from major lutein-rich food groups, and consumption of those lutein-rich food groups themselves are associated with open-angle glaucoma (OAG) and related ocular parameters.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from The Maastricht Study.
PARTICIPANTS: Community-dwelling adults aged 40-75 years (N = 5,613), including 442 participants with OAG.
METHODS: Dietary intake over the preceding year was assessed using a validated food-frequency questionnaire to estimate total dietary lutein intake, source-specific lutein intake (from vegetables, fruit, eggs, and nuts), and consumption of these foods. Glaucoma was classified from standard automated perimetry (Heidelberg Edge Perimeter) with independent specialist review. Intraocular pressure (IOP) was measured by non-contact tonometry, and retinal structural parameters (peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer and ganglion cell complex) were obtained by spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT). Eye-level generalized and linear mixed-effects models with participant-level random intercepts were used, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and metabolic covariates.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Open-angle glaucoma, IOP, and OCT-derived retinal layer thicknesses.
RESULTS: Total dietary lutein intake was not significantly associated with OAG prevalence (odds ratio [OR] per standard deviation [SD] increase, 0.97; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.87-1.09). Among source-specific lutein analyses, only lutein derived from nuts was associated with lower odds of OAG (OR, 0.86; 95%CI, 0.75-0.98 per SD increase), whereas lutein derived from vegetables, fruit, and eggs was not. In the analyses of lutein-rich food group consumption, higher vegetable intake (OR, 0.84; 95%CI, 0.75-0.95 per SD increase) and higher nut intake (OR, 0.86; 95%CI, 0.75-0.98 per SD increase) were each associated with lower odds of OAG, whereas fruit and egg intake were not. Neither dietary lutein intake nor consumption of lutein-rich food were associated with IOP or OCT structural measures.
CONCLUSIONS: Total dietary lutein intake was not significantly associated with OAG prevalence, whereas higher vegetable and nut intakes were associated with lower odds of OAG. These findings support examining total dietary and source-specific lutein intake alongside consumption of the lutein-rich foods.

etudes.titre: The association between sedentary behavior and eye diseases: a prospective study from the UK Biobank.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Sedentary behavior (SB) is a well-established risk factor for multiple chronic diseases. However, evidence regarding its association with common ocular disorders remains limited and inconsistent. This study investigated the prospective associations between SB and the risks of incident age-related macular degeneration (AMD), glaucoma, dry eye disease (DED), and retinal vein occlusion (RVO).
METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort analysis using data from the UK Biobank. Separate analytical cohorts were established for AMD (n = 374,552), glaucoma (n = 370,997), DED (n = 374,398), and RVO (n = 374,924). During a median follow-up of approximately 14.04 years, 7,266 AMD, 8,112 glaucoma, 452 DED, and 786 RVO cases were identified. Pre-existing ocular diseases were identified using ICD-10 records and self-reported diagnoses. Incident AMD, glaucoma, and RVO were identified from ICD-10 records, whereas incident DED was identified by self-report. Cox proportional hazards models, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses, interaction analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: In unadjusted models, higher SB was associated with increased risks of AMD, glaucoma, DED and RVO. After multivariable adjustment, only a borderline statistically significant association remained for AMD (HR = 1.01; 95% CI: 1.00-1.02), whereas no significant associations were observed for glaucoma, DED, or RVO. RCS analyses demonstrated mild J-shaped associations between SB and AMD and glaucoma, with the lowest risk observed at approximately 3.7 h/day; however, these associations became nonsignificant after full adjustment. Stratified interaction analyses identified significant effect modification for AMD by body mass index (BMI), glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), and physical activity (PA) level, and for DED by sex and BMI. Sensitivity analyses, including additional adjustment for physical activity and sleep duration and analyses of domain-specific sedentary behaviors, did not alter the overall conclusions.
CONCLUSION: After adjustment for potential confounders, no statistically significant independent associations were observed between SB and incident AMD, glaucoma, DED, or RVO. However, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence against a causal relationship. Further studies incorporating objective exposure assessment, repeated measurements, and causal inference approaches are warranted to clarify the potential role of sedentary behavior in ocular disease development.

etudes.titre: Circumferential Identification of Peripheral Anterior Synechiae by Air-Puff Dynamic Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Optical Coherence Tomography »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to objectively and accurately identify peripheral anterior synechiae (PAS) circumferentially in eyes with angle-closure glaucoma (ACG).
METHODS: Anterior chamber angles (ACAs) were classified as PAS or non-PAS (NPAS) groups by indentation gonioscopy. A custom-built air-puff dynamic anterior segment optical coherence tomography (DAS-OCT) system with an innovative 4-leaf clover-scan pattern acquired 10 frames per ACA along 8 radial directions at 45-degree intervals within 65 ms. Dynamic parameters including the differences in angle opening distance at 750 µm from the scleral spur (AOD750) and trabecular-iris space area at 750 µm anterior to the scleral spur (TISA750) before and after air-puff stimulation, were extracted to establish a binary logistic regression model. Model performance was evaluated in the testing set.
RESULTS: Analysis of 68 images from 9 healthy eyes confirmed high measurement repeatability (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.821 for AOD750dif; 0.775 for TISA750dif). A total of 143 anterior segment OCT (AS-OCT) images from 20 ACG eyes were analyzed, with 100 assigned to the training set and 43 to the testing set. Significant differences in AOD750dif and TISA750dif were identified between the NPAS and PAS groups (P < 0.001). The dual-parameter model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.924 in the training set and 0.913 in the testing set, with an overall accuracy of 83.7%.
CONCLUSIONS: The air-puff DAS-OCT system enables the noninvasive, dynamic, and circumferential identification of PAS, demonstrating high diagnostic performance.
TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE: This non-contact imaging technology offers a quantitative alternative to indentation gonioscopy, potentially improving ACG screening efficiency and guiding clinical management.

etudes.titre: Periorbital Fat Loss From Prostaglandin Analogues: Dermatologic and Cosmetic Considerations.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Topical prostaglandin (PG) analogues, originally developed as first-line therapies for glaucoma, are increasingly used in dermatology and cosmetic settings to promote eyelash and eyebrow growth. However, their use has been associated with prostaglandin-associated periorbitopathy (PAP), a constellation of adverse effects including periorbital fat atrophy, deepening of the upper eyelid sulcus, ptosis, and skin hyperpigmentation. These changes can be subtle but carry significant aesthetic and psychosocial consequences, particularly in patients using PG analogues for cosmetic enhancement.
AIMS: This review aims to synthesize current knowledge on the clinical features, pathophysiology, and reversibility of PAP, with an emphasis on implications for dermatologic practice.
METHODS: A narrative review of the literature was conducted using PubMed, focusing on dermatologic, ophthalmologic, and cosmetic reports related to PG analogue use and PAP.
RESULTS: Although PAP is well recognized in ophthalmology, dermatology-specific data remain sparse. Many over-the-counter eyelash serums contain PG analogues yet lack accurate labeling and regulatory oversight. Diagnostic delays are common, and dermatologists may overlook serum use as a contributing factor in periorbital changes.
CONCLUSIONS: As the off-label and consumer-driven use of PG analogues continues to rise, dermatologists must remain vigilant in identifying PAP. Routine history-taking should include inquiry about eyelash and eyebrow serums. Greater regulatory oversight, patient education, and dermatology-focused research are needed to promote safe and informed use.

etudes.titre: Bidirectional associations between glaucoma and skin neoplasms: a global retrospective cohort study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Glaucoma and skin neoplasms are common disorders in older adults, but whether they are longitudinally associated remains unclear. Biological links have been proposed based on shared susceptibility to oxidative injury and ultraviolet radiation. We used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network to examine the relationship between glaucoma and skin neoplasms in both temporal directions. After propensity score matching, the glaucoma analysis included 873,294 patients in each cohort. Glaucoma was associated with a higher subsequent risk of skin neoplasms (HR 1.220; 95% CI 1.185-1.256), with similar findings for melanoma (HR 1.197; 95% CI 1.101-1.301) and non-melanoma skin cancer (HR 1.228; 95% CI 1.191-1.266). In analyses stratified by race, the association was observed among White patients (HR 1.274; 95% CI 1.233-1.317), but did not reach statistical significance among Black or Asian patients. The reciprocal analysis included 1,456,093 patients in each matched cohort. A history of skin neoplasms was associated with subsequent glaucoma (HR 1.881; 95% CI 1.841-1.922), and the association remained significant across the racial groups examined. Several glaucoma-related conditions also showed elevated risks, including glaucoma suspect states. Our findings demonstrate longitudinal associations between glaucoma and skin neoplasms in both directions. The results may increase clinical awareness of these coexisting conditions, although the observational design does not establish causality or justify routine cross-specialty screening. Further studies are needed to determine the mechanisms underlying these associations and whether risk-based surveillance has clinical value.

etudes.titre: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and the Risk of Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Agonists »
etudes.resume:
TOPIC: Whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use is associated with a lower risk of incident glaucoma or ocular hypertension (OHT) in adults, and whether the association differs by diabetes status or comparator.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, and every licensed treatment targets lowering intraocular pressure (IOP); none protects retinal ganglion cells directly. GLP-1RAs are widely prescribed and have been proposed to be neuroprotective, so whether this class of medication alters glaucoma risk matters at prescribing and to the search for pressure-independent treatment. Four earlier meta-analyses found no significant association but pooled non-equivalent comparators.
METHODS: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies, following PRISMA 2020 and registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251082642). PubMed was searched on 15 April 2026 and updated to 30 August 2026, with CENTRAL, Europe PMC, the first 100 Google Scholar results and bidirectional citation tracking as supplementary sources. Eligible studies were retrospective cohort or nested case-control studies of GLP-1RA exposure with incident glaucoma, OHT or IOP change as the outcome and with adjustment for confounding. Two reviewers screened, extracted and applied ROBINS-I. Estimates were pooled by DerSimonian-Laird random effects, with a Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) interval, a 95% prediction interval and GRADE.
RESULTS: Ten studies were included from 406 screened records. Six cohorts covering 225,814 matched or analysed patients were pooled. GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower incidence of recorded glaucoma or OHT (pooled hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.80; HKSJ CI 0.56 to 0.85), but heterogeneity was 58.5%, the 95% prediction interval (0.44 to 1.08) included no effect, and certainty was low. The association held after all TriNetX studies were removed (0.78, 0.71 to 0.85) and after restriction to open-angle outcomes (0.66, 0.53 to 0.82). Diabetes status, comparator type and data platform could not be separated.
CONCLUSION: Low-certainty observational evidence suggests GLP-1RA use is not associated with a higher risk of glaucoma or OHT and may be associated with a lower one. Confounding by indication, coded outcome ascertainment and a prediction interval that includes no effect mean protection has not been shown. The findings support reassurance and the randomized trial under way.

etudes.titre: Vitreous vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 levels in vitreoretinal pathologies: a prospective analysis of 181 eyes.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To quantify vitreous vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1) across vitreoretinal pathologies and identify associated factors.
DESIGN: Prospective, single-centre, cross-sectional observational study.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 181 eyes of 171 adults undergoing pars plana vitrectomy (PPV).
METHODS: Undiluted midvitreous specimens were aspirated before infusion. Eyes were formed into 5 subgroups: advanced proliferative diabetic retinopathy (n = 80), rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (n = 65), vitreomacular interface (VMI) disease (n = 17), retained lens fragments (n = 14), and endophthalmitis (n = 5). VCAM-1 was measured by sandwich enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. VMI disease was the reference category; no disease-free controls existed. Log-transformed VCAM-1 was analysed by univariable and multivariable regression with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate adjustment.
RESULTS: VCAM-1 differed across subgroups (P < 0.001), greatest in endophthalmitis (45 972.61 ± SE 22 130.67 pg/mL; n = 5) and lowest in VMI disease (3669.46 ± 642.42 pg/mL). Chronic kidney disease (P = 0.031) and longer duration of diabetes (unstandardised coefficient B = 411.15 ± 173.65 pg/mL per year; P = 0.020) were associated with greater VCAM-1, although neither group survived false discovery rate adjustment (q = 0.109 and 0.093). Pre-existing glaucoma was independently associated with elevated VCAM-1 (20 126.36 ± 4784.77 vs 9946.15 ± 1147.22 pg/mL; P = 0.003; q = 0.021).
CONCLUSIONS: Vitreous VCAM-1 varied across vitreoretinal diagnoses, greatest in endophthalmitis, although on only 5 eyes. Longer duration of diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and pre-existing glaucoma were each associated with greater VCAM-1. These cross-sectional associations are hypothesis-generating and do not establish a mechanistic or causal role.
etudes.revue: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie

etudes.titre: Clinical Outcomes of Bio-Interventional Cyclodialysis with One or Multiple Allogeneic Reinforcements: A Multicenter Real-World Evidence Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
INTRODUCTION: Bio-reinforced cyclodialysis uses a biocompatible acellular scleral allograft spacer to maintain a surgically created cleft and enhance uveoscleral outflow. The titratable effect of one vs two spacers on intraocular pressure (IOP) lowering has not previously been evaluated.
METHODS: Analysis of 260 eyes (187 patients) in the prospective, multicenter CREST study (NCT05506423) undergoing combined phacoemulsification and bio-reinforced cyclodialysis with one spacer (N = 146) or two (N = 114). The primary endpoint was IOP change from baseline to month 12. Analyses comprised unadjusted comparison, baseline-adjusted regression, 1:1 propensity score matching, doubly robust overlap weighting, and models accounting for enrolling site and fellow eyes. IOP after a secondary IOP-lowering procedure was censored. IOP reported as mean (95% CI) and medications as mean (± SD).
RESULTS: At baseline, IOP was 17.8 (4.2) vs 18.5 (5.7) mmHg and medications 1.3 (1.1) vs 1.5 (1.4), with one vs two spacers, respectively. Enrolling site was most imbalanced: one center contributed 38.6% of two-spacer eyes but 7.5% of one-spacer eyes. The unadjusted difference in IOP reduction was 2.5 mmHg (1.2-3.8; p < 0.001) and persisted after propensity score matching (2.4 mmHg; 0.9-3.8; p = 0.001) and overlap weighting (2.0 mmHg; 1.2-2.8; p < 0.001). After accounting for site, it attenuated to 0.9 mmHg (- 0.1 to 1.8; p = 0.080), and to 0.4 mmHg (- 0.6 to 1.5; p = 0.424) using both strategies. Medication reduction (- 0.7 vs - 0.6; p = 0.643), freedom from secondary incisional surgery (98.6% vs 99.1%), and site-adjusted adverse event rates did not differ.
CONCLUSION: Two-spacer treatment was associated with numerically greater 12-month IOP reduction in unadjusted and patient-level adjusted analyses, but this association was substantially attenuated after accounting for enrolling site. These short-term real-world data are compatible with, but do not establish, an independent incremental effect of a second spacer. Further study is warranted.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05506423.

etudes.titre: Retinal Organotypic Cultures as an Ex Vivo Platform to Study Ocular Diseases: Advantages, Challenges, and Translational Perspective.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Retinal organotypic cultures represent a useful ex vivo platform that bridges the gap between traditional in vitro cell cultures and complex in vivo animal models. This ex vivo model uniquely preserves native tissue architecture, including laminar organization and essential neuron-glia interactions, while providing a controlled environment that enables precise manipulation of experimental variables such as oxygen levels, glucose concentrations, and drug exposure. Recent methodological advances have significantly enhanced the reproducibility and translational relevance of retinal organotypic cultures, thereby enabling their use as robust models for studying major blinding disorders, including glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and diabetic retinopathy (DR). Furthermore, the development of co-culture systems with the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) has improved the modeling of the outer retinal microenvironment and photoreceptor survival. Nevertheless, the absence of systemic vascular and immune influences, the short-term viability, and the progressive functional decline constrain the application of these systems for investigating the slow, age-dependent progression of chronic retinal diseases. Overall, organotypic retinal cultures represent a valuable complementary tool in preclinical ophthalmic research, and continued methodological refinement is expected to further enhance their translational relevance for both common and inherited retinal disorders.

etudes.titre: Intraocular Pressure Change After Cataract Surgery in Normal-Tension Glaucoma and Nonglaucomatous Eyes: Predictors of Postoperative Response.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Surgery »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the intraocular pressure (IOP) changes after cataract surgery between medically treated normal-tension glaucoma (NTG) and nonglaucomatous eyes and identify factors associated with a ≥10% IOP reduction in the overall cohort.
SETTING: Yonsei University Health System.
DESIGN: Retrospective comparative cohort study.
METHODS: We analyzed 292 eyes (203 nonglaucomatous, 89 NTG) undergoing uncomplicated cataract surgery with ≥6 months of follow-up. NTG eyes maintained unchanged glaucoma medication regimens. IOP was measured preoperatively and at 1, 2, and 6 months. IOP reduction rates were analyzed with a linear mixed-effects model. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of a ≥10% IOP reduction at 6 months. An exploratory nomogram was developed in the overall cohort and internally validated using 200 bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: At 6 months, IOP decreased from 13.45 ± 3.15 to 12.09 ± 2.70 mmHg in nonglaucomatous eyes (p < 0.001), whereas the change from 12.81 ± 3.01 to 12.04 ± 2.84 mmHg in NTG eyes was not significant (p = 0.139). The group-by-time interaction was not significant (p = 0.763). In the overall cohort, higher preoperative IOP (OR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.35-1.71), shallower anterior chamber depth (OR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.08-0.57), and older age (OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.01-1.09) were independently associated with achieving a ≥10% IOP reduction. The nomogram showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.801) and acceptable internal calibration.
CONCLUSIONS: Cataract surgery significantly reduced IOP in nonglaucomatous eyes. Although the mean 6-month reduction was not significant in medically treated NTG eyes, responses varied substantially. In the overall cohort, preoperative characteristics may help identify eyes more likely to benefit.
etudes.revue: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

etudes.titre: Intersectional fairness in vision-language models for medical image disease classification.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) systems, particularly multimodal vision-language models (VLM), often exhibit intersectional biases, with models systematically less confident in diagnosing marginalised patient subgroups and producing higher rates of missed diagnoses. Current fairness interventions frequently fail to address these gaps or compromise overall diagnostic performance to achieve statistical parity. In this study, we developed Cross-Modal Alignment Consistency (CMAC-MMD), a training framework that standardises diagnostic certainty across intersectional patient subgroups without requiring sensitive demographic data during clinical inference. We evaluated this approach using 10,015 skin lesion images (HAM10000) with external validation on 12,000 images (BCN20000), and 10,000 fundus images for glaucoma detection (Harvard-FairVLMed), stratifying performance by intersectional age, gender, and race attributes. In the dermatology cohort, the proposed method reduced the overall intersectional missed diagnosis gap (difference in True Positive Rate, ΔTPR) from 0.50 to 0.26 while improving the Area Under the Curve (AUC) from 0.94 to 0.97 compared to standard training. Similarly, for glaucoma screening, the method reduced ΔTPR from 0.41 to 0.31, achieving a better AUC of 0.72 (vs. 0.71 baseline). This provides a methodological foundation toward clinical decision support systems that are both accurate and perform more equitably across diverse patient subgroups, without increasing privacy risks during inference.

etudes.titre: Trends in initial glaucoma surgery for patients with primary open angle glaucoma from 2015 to 2025: a national database study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgery »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate national trends in first-line surgical management of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) from 2015 to 2025.
METHODS: Data were analyzed from the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network. Procedures were identified by CPT codes and categorized into four groups: angle-based MIGS, trabeculectomy, aqueous shunts, or transscleral cyclophotocoagulation (TSCPC). Patients with prior glaucoma procedures were excluded. Annual proportions of each surgery type were calculated, and temporal trends were assessed using the Cochran-Armitage test.
RESULTS: 23,521 adult patients with a diagnosis of POAG received an initial glaucoma surgery during the time period. 14,606 patients underwent angle-based MIGS, 3,374 underwent trabeculectomy, 4,027 underwent aqueous shunt, and 1,514 underwent TSCPC. The MIGS cohort had the highest proportion of mild POAG, and lowest baseline medication (P < 0.0001). From 2015 to 2025, initial angle-based MIGS increased significantly from 22.09% to 72.28% (P < 0.0001). During the same period, initial trabeculectomy decreased from 38.00% to 8.71% (P < 0.0001) and initial aqueous shunt implantation decreased from 33.06% to 14.40% (P < 0.0001). No significant change occurred in the proportion of patients receiving initial TSCPC (P = 0.18).
CONCLUSIONS: Between 2015 and 2025, the total number of glaucoma surgeries performed in the United States increased significantly, and angle-based MIGS became the predominant first-line surgical intervention for POAG. Although the proportion of trabeculectomy and aqueous shunt implantation declined, the rise in MIGS does not necessarily indicate a shift away from traditional glaucoma surgery. Patients undergoing MIGS tended to have milder disease and lower baseline medication burden, suggesting that this trend may primarily reflect the use of MIGS at earlier disease stages, likely owing to their more favorable safety profile compared with traditional filtering surgeries.
