etudes.titre: Estimating selected screening-related parameters using New Zealand-specific glaucoma prevalence data: optometry visits for glaucoma screening at age 45 years.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « screening »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Regular eye examinations for glaucoma at age 45 years and every 5 years after have been promoted in the New Zealand setting. We aimed to estimate selected screening-related parameters for optometry visits for glaucoma screening at age 45 years.
METHODS: Selected glaucoma screening parameters were identified from the literature, and data were extracted from a New Zealand longitudinal study (Dunedin Study) on the prevalence of glaucoma in 45-year-olds. Out-of-pocket costs were estimated from New Zealand optometry assessment fees.
RESULTS: We estimate that routine screening for glaucoma within a New Zealand cohort of 45-year-olds has a low positive predictive value of 5.4%. That is, for every 100 people who get a positive screening result for glaucoma, around 95 of these diagnoses would be expected to be false positives and only five would truly have glaucoma. The number needed to screen to detect one case of glaucoma was estimated at 177. The out-of-pocket cost per true case of glaucoma detected was around NZ$24,300, equivalent to NZ$5.8 million at the national level to detect 241 true cases per year (assuming 70% uptake). However, there would be many other additional costs likely with any formal screening programme encompassing the full clinical pathway.
CONCLUSION: These New Zealand-specific findings for selected screening parameters align with recommendations from international agencies showing that there is a lack of evidence in favour of population screening for glaucoma. Future research could focus on evaluating more targeted screening or risk-based screening, e.g., using artificial intelligence-assisted fundus imaging.

etudes.titre: Clonal hematopoiesis and the risk of major age-related eye diseases.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), an age-related hematologic condition associated with systemic inflammation, has uncertain associations with major eye diseases. We aimed to investigate the association of CHIP, including its major genetic subtypes and clone sizes, with the risk of cataract, glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and diabetic retinopathy (DR). UK Biobank participants enrolled during 2006-2010 were followed by linked electronic health records until March 2022. Whole-exome sequencing identified CHIP as somatic driver mutations with variant allele frequency ≥ 2%. Multivariable Cox regression was applied to assess hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CI). The DR analysis was restricted to participants with diabetes. Of 436,469 participants (mean age, 56.4 years; 54.5% women), 14,110 (3.2%) had CHIP. During a median 14.4-year follow-up, 31,165 cataract, 12,393 glaucoma, 13,644 AMD, and 2,692 DR diagnoses occurred. CHIP was associated with cataract (HR [95%CI]: 1.08 [1.03-1.14]), AMD (HR [95%CI]: 1.12 [1.04-1.21]), and DR (HR [95%CI]: 1.48 [1.25-1.74]), but the association with glaucoma overall did not reach statistical significance (HR [95%CI]: 1.08 [0.99-1.17]). The glaucoma association was statistically significant among participants without hypertension (HR [95%CI]: 1.22 [1.06-1.40]; P for interaction = 0.012). Associations varied by clone size and driver gene. Hematologic and inflammatory biomarkers mediated less than 5% of associations. CHIP was associated with incident cataract, AMD, and DR, and with glaucoma in participants without hypertension. These findings position CHIP as a potential non-ocular risk marker for several major age-related eye diseases. However, except for DR, effect sizes were small.

etudes.titre: [Risk-adapted aftercare of glaucoma-Between patient safety, treatment quality and resource efficiency : Fewer controls for glaucoma-Is that possible? Less is more? How much monitoring is really necessary in chronic eye diseases?].
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « monitoring »
etudes.resume: The number of patients with glaucoma continues to increase as a consequence of demographic change. At the same time, ophthalmological healthcare systems are facing growing economic constraints and workforce shortages. Against this background, the question of whether follow-up examinations can be reduced has gained increasing attention; however, the goal should not be a blanket reduction in follow-up visits but rather a risk-adapted, evidence-based approach to determining appropriate monitoring intervals. National and international clinical guidelines support extending follow-up intervals in patients with stable glaucoma, whereas close monitoring remains essential following initial diagnosis, treatment modifications or documented disease progression. This review discusses the available scientific evidence, summarizes recommendations from relevant clinical guidelines and highlights future developments toward individualized follow-up strategies.

etudes.titre: Outcomes of Initial Surgical Treatment of Neovascular Glaucoma with Tube Shunt or Transscleral Cyclophotocoagulation: A Retrospective, Comparative Study.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Shunt »; mot du titre : « Tube »
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To compare 6-month outcomes of eyes with neovascular glaucoma (NVG) that underwent tube shunt implantation or transscleral cyclophotocoagulation (CPC).
DESIGN: Single-institution retrospective comparative study.
SUBJECTS: Adult patients with NVG who underwent tube shunt surgery or CPC.
METHODS: Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics of patients with NVG who underwent tube shunt or CPC between January 1, 2016, to December 31, 2024, were extracted from the electronic health record (EHR). A doubly robust approach combining inverse probability weighting (IPW) with covariate adjustment was used to account for measured baseline differences between surgical groups. Generalized estimating equation (GEE) models were used for binary and longitudinal outcomes, accounting for within-patient correlation, and Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event outcomes. Results were reported as risk ratios (RRs) or hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Surgical failure, defined as reoperation within 6 months, intraocular pressure (IOP) failure (>21 mmHg or <6 mmHg with clinical hypotony), or loss of light perception, was the primary outcome.
RESULTS: Among 222 eyes, 145 underwent CPC and 77 underwent tube shunt implantation. CPC-treated eyes had worse preoperative visual acuity (≤20/200 in 86.2% vs 49.4%), higher IOP (≥49 mmHg in 36.6% vs 10.4%), and more severe-stage glaucoma (63.4% vs 44.2%) than tube shunt eyes. The overall composite failure rate was 51.4%, occurring in 74 CPC-treated eyes (51.0%) and 40 tube shunt eyes (51.9%). IPW-GEE analysis showed no significant difference in composite surgical failure between CPC and tube shunt surgery (RR=0.94, 95%CI: 0.71-1.39; p=0.95). Although unadjusted Kaplan-Meier analyses suggested higher risks of composite surgical failure and loss of light perception among CPC-treated eyes, these associations were attenuated after IPW, with no statistically significant differences in time to composite failure (HR=1.38, 95%CI: 0.83-2.28; p=0.22), reoperation (HR=1.62, 95%CI: 0.59-4.44; p=0.35), loss of light perception (HR=1.87, 95%CI: 0.86-4.05; p=0.11), or IOP failure (HR=1.71, 95%CI: 0.81-3.61; p=0.16).
CONCLUSIONS: After IPW adjustment for substantial measured baseline differences, we found no significant differences in surgical outcomes between CPC and tube shunt surgery for NVG. However, residual confounding by unmeasured factors remains possible, warranting cautious interpretation.

etudes.titre: Progressive corneal denervation in Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma with female-predominant corneal remodeling.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma is characterized by anterior segment dysgenesis, ocular hypertension, and optic neuropathy, but its consequences for corneal sensory innervation remain poorly defined. We examined male and female Pitx2egl1/egl1 and Pitx2+/+ mice at 1 and 3 months using intraocular pressure measurements, fundus imaging, visual evoked potentials, optic nerve ultrastructure, corneal βIII-tubulin whole-mount imaging, mechanical sensitivity testing, and bulk RNA sequencing of corneas and trigeminal ganglia. Mutant mice developed ocular hypertension, posterior segment abnormalities, reduced visual evoked potential amplitudes, and optic nerve degeneration. Corneal epithelial nerve fiber volume was preserved at 1 month but reduced in both sexes at 3 months, indicating progressive denervation in an untreated genetic model. Mechanical sensitivity was reduced in mutant males, whereas female values did not differ detectably between genotypes. Factorial transcriptomic analysis included sex, genotype, and their interaction. Female mutant corneas showed 634 strict differentially expressed genes, with enrichment of complement, cytokine, extracellular matrix, focal adhesion, p53-related, glycan, and metabolic pathways. No comparably robust gene set was detected in male corneas. Additional diagnostics indicated small male genotype effects at the gene level and a diffuse aggregate sex-conditioned signal that was not resolved at single-gene false-discovery-rate level. Whole-mount KRT17 immunolabeling showed expansion of the KRT17-positive epithelial domain in female mutant corneas, providing orthogonal spatial support for an epithelial remodeling component of this signature. Whole-trigeminal-ganglion bulk RNA-seq detected few significant changes, but dilution of cornea-projecting neurons within the whole ganglion precludes concluding that these neurons were unresponsive. These findings identify progressive corneal denervation as an underrecognized component of Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma and define female-predominant corneal remodeling as a hypothesis-generating molecular feature rather than a proven sex-specific mechanism.

etudes.titre: Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization Analysis of the Causal Relationships Between Psychiatric Disorders and Glaucoma-Related Traits.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To reveal the causality between psychiatric disorders and glaucoma-related traits.
PARTICIPANTS: Genomewide association studies of glaucoma-related traits including primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), intraocular pressure (IOP), retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness, and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) thickness involving European participants were used. GWAS data for psychiatric disorders, including bipolar disorder (BD), anxiety, major depressive disorder, and schizophrenia (SCZ), were extracted from European patients.
METHODS: Bidirectional univariable Mendelian randomization (UVMR) was conducted using the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method to evaluate causal relationships between glaucoma-related traits and psychiatric disorders. Sensitivity analyses, including Cochran's Q test, the MR-Egger intercept test, leave-one-out analyses, and funnel plots, were used to detect potential horizontal pleiotropy.
RESULTS: Significant causal associations were identified between IOP and SCZ (β = 0.0410, 95% CI: 0.0139-0.0681, p = 0.003). No causal relationships were found for other glaucoma-related traits on psychiatric disorders and psychiatric disorders on glaucoma-related traits.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study shows that elevated IOP causally increases the risk of SCZ, while no causal links were found between glaucoma traits and BD, MDD, or anxiety. These findings suggest that lowering IOP could reduce SCZ risk, offering new insights into the connection between glaucoma and psychiatric disorders.

etudes.titre: Artificial intelligence for detecting and predicting glaucomatous progression.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Artificial intelligence »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines the current state of artificial intelligence (AI) models for the detection and prediction of glaucomatous progression.
RECENT FINDINGS: Machine learning and deep learning models have been developed to analyze longitudinal data from optic disc photographs, optical coherence tomography images, and visual field tests to identify worsening glaucoma. Recent AI research has also expanded beyond simply detecting progression to predicting future disease trajectories. These approaches may provide more efficient assessment than clinician review alone.
SUMMARY: AI models can rapidly analyze large volumes of clinical data to support individualized glaucoma management; these models can guide treatment intensity and follow-up intervals by detecting and predicting glaucomatous progression. However, significant hurdles to clinical adoption remain, including the "black box" nature of AI, absence of a universally accepted reference standard for progression, variable data quality, and limited generalizability across populations and clinical settings. AI is poised to function as a clinical decision support tool rather than a replacement for clinicians. Prospective studies are needed to determine the impact of AI in improving patient outcomes, clinical efficiency, and healthcare costs.

etudes.titre: Role of Corneal Biomechanics in the Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Management of Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Diagnosis »; mot du titre : « Biomechanics »
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Corneal biomechanical properties exert profound influences on glaucoma pathogenesis, diagnosis, and clinical management. These tissue characteristics not only interfere with the accuracy of intraocular pressure (IOP) measurement but also independently correlate with glaucoma onset and progressive optic nerve damage.
MAIN TEXT: This narrative review focuses on two core corneal biomechanical parameters, corneal hysteresis (CH) and corneal resistance factor (CRF), and elaborates their inherent associations with glaucoma. We discuss how abnormal corneal biomechanics participate in glaucomatous pathological changes and further summarize their clinical value in early diagnosis, disease progression monitoring, and personalized glaucoma treatment.
CONCLUSION: By integrating the latest research advances, this review provides solid theoretical support for routine clinical practice and proposes directions for subsequent research, which will promote broader clinical translation of corneal biomechanical detection in glaucoma management.

etudes.titre: Surgically induced astigmatism after phacotrabeculectomy: a prospective observational study at ECWA Eye Hospital, Kano.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Combined phacotrabeculectomy is commonly performed in patients with coexisting cataract and primary open angle glaucoma to achieve simultaneous visual rehabilitation and intraocular pressure control. However, the procedure may induce corneal astigmatic changes that influence postoperative visual outcomes. This study prospectively evaluated the magnitude and temporal changes of surgically induced astigmatism following phacotrabeculectomy using both arithmetic and vector analytic methods.
METHODS: This hospital based prospective observational study was conducted at ECWA Eye Hospital, Kano, Nigeria, between July 2024 and June 2025. Adults aged 40 years or older with visually significant age-related cataract and primary open angle glaucoma who underwent single site superior phacotrabeculectomy were enrolled and followed for 12 weeks. Corneal astigmatism was measured preoperatively and at postoperative weeks 1, 6, and 12. Surgically induced astigmatism was calculated using arithmetic subtraction and vector analysis based on the Alpins method. Temporal changes in surgically induced astigmatism and intraocular pressure were evaluated using linear mixed effects modeling.
RESULTS: Sixty-three participants completed follow up. Mean arithmetic surgically induced astigmatism decreased from 1.46 ± 0.90 D at week 1 to 0.03 ± 0.81 D at week 12. Mean vector surgically induced astigmatism decreased from 2.41 ± 1.54 D to 1.52 ± 0.96 D over the same period. Centroid astigmatism reduced progressively over time. Linear mixed model analysis demonstrated a significant effect of time on surgically induced astigmatism (F (2,124) = 16.89, p < 0.001). Vector analysis yielded greater magnitudes than the arithmetic method (p = 0.001). Intraocular pressure decreased from 18.89 ± 4.81 mmHg preoperatively to 14.63 ± 3.46 mmHg at week 12 (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Phacotrabeculectomy is associated with an early increase in corneal astigmatism followed by gradual reduction over time, with a trend toward relative stabilization by 12 weeks. Vector analysis provides a more comprehensive assessment of surgically induced astigmatism than arithmetic subtraction by accounting for changes in both magnitude and axis. These findings support appropriate timing of postoperative refractive assessment and highlight the relevance of preoperative astigmatism when considering refractive planning in combined cataract and glaucoma surgery.

etudes.titre: Recent advances in optical coherence tomography for glaucoma: from macular imaging and optical coherence tomography angiography to artificial intelligence and portable platforms.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « artificial intelligence »; mot du titre : « optical coherence tomography »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Recent advances are extending optical coherence tomography (OCT)'s role beyond conventional structural metrics. This review summarizes recent developments in macular OCT, OCT angiography (OCTA), artificial intelligence (AI), and portable/home-based OCT.
RECENT FINDINGS: Macular ganglion-cell measures (ganglion-cell-inner plexiform layer, ganglion cell complex) increasingly complement retinal nerve fiber layer assessment, offering greater diagnostic/prognostic value in advanced glaucoma, myopia, and certain glaucoma subtypes. OCTA is emerging as a complementary vascular biomarker; peripapillary vessel density shows the most consistent link to progression, with early evidence that vascular changes may precede detectable structural or functional decline. Deep learning models increasingly use raw or multimodal imaging rather than summary parameters; foundation and multimodal architectures (e.g., RETFound-based) show strong diagnostic performance and improved generalizability across demographics and disease severity. However, AI-based progression prediction remains less robust than cross-sectional diagnosis, especially under external validation. Portable/home-based OCT may extend monitoring beyond the clinic, though clinical utility remains investigational.
SUMMARY: The field is moving toward multimodal, longitudinal, AI-supported glaucoma assessment integrating structural, vascular, and functional biomarkers rather than interpreting them in isolation. Key priorities for translation include standardized acquisition and analysis across devices, large and diverse external validation cohorts, interpretable models, and evidence that AI and remote imaging improve clinically meaningful outcomes. These developments should make OCT increasingly central to earlier detection and individualized monitoring of glaucoma, but none currently replace established structural and functional assessment or clinical judgment.

etudes.titre: Blood pressure and glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Intraocular pressure (IOP) remains the only modifiable risk factor in glaucoma, yet many patients continue to progress despite adequate IOP control. Systemic blood pressure (BP) has re-emerged as a candidate IOP-independent vascular risk factor. This review synthesizes current evidence on the relationship between BP and glaucoma, with particular attention to recent literature describing circadian BP patterns, short- and long-term BP variability, and minimum ambulatory BP values.
RECENT FINDINGS: Both elevated and reduced BP have been associated with glaucoma development and progression, consistent with a bimodal relationship mediated by ocular perfusion pressure. Beyond absolute BP level, recent studies using 24-h ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM) have identified nocturnal over-dipping, high 24-h and long-term BP variability, and, most notably, the minimum BP nadir as independent predictors of structural and functional glaucomatous progression, often outperforming mean BP values in multivariable models. Office-based BP measurements correlate poorly with 24-h ABPM specifically among patients with the lowest BP readings, suggesting isolated office readings may fail to capture clinically relevant hypotensive exposure. Emerging evidence further indicates that BP-related vulnerability is not uniform across the eye: the focal ischemic optic disc phenotype and the central visual field each appear disproportionately susceptible to the effects of low or unstable BP compared with generalized cup enlargement phenotypes or the peripheral field, respectively.
SUMMARY: The relationship between BP and glaucoma is more complex than a simple linear or threshold-based association, encompassing absolute level, circadian pattern, variability, and minimum values, each of which may independently influence disease course. Twenty-four-hour ABPM may offer meaningful prognostic value beyond office-based measurement, particularly in patients progressing despite controlled IOP, and clinicians should maintain a low threshold to pursue such monitoring and to coordinate BP management with primary care or cardiology colleagues in this population.

etudes.resume:
BACKGROUND: Patient-reported quality of life during routine use of mobile medication-support applications in glaucoma is poorly characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize longitudinal health-related quality of life among self-selected OcuDrop users and explore associated factors.
METHODS: This single-center prospective observational cohort included adults with glaucoma or ocular hypertension recruited through a clinic announcement that specified Android-only availability. Participants voluntarily used the medication-reminder application during routine care. EQ-5D-5L was assessed at baseline and months 1, 2, and 3; NEI-VFQ-25 was exploratory. Random-intercept mixed models evaluated change over time. App events were linked using pseudonymous identifiers.
RESULTS: Of 81 voluntary app users, 64 enrolled and 54 had EQ-5D-5L data at all visits. Mean utility was 0.681 at baseline, 0.730 at month 1, 0.777 at month 2, and 0.775 at month 3 (overall P = 0.001). The month-3 within-person change was 0.094 (95% CI: 0.030 to 0.159; Cohen dz = 0.40); clinical importance could not be determined because no applicable glaucoma-specific Thai minimal clinically important difference was identified. Older age was associated with lower baseline utility, and baseline utility with month-3 utility, in exploratory models. Among 54 participants, 50 generated at least one app event and 39 generated an event in month 3. Ten enrolled participants had no available EQ-5D-5L records data and used more topical medications than included participants.
CONCLUSION: EQ-5D-5L utility increased over three months among self-selected users, but the uncontrolled design, Android-only eligibility, missing outcomes, and variable engagement preclude attribution to OcuDrop. Findings are hypothesis-generating.

etudes.titre: Relationship Between Chromatic Sensitivity and Retinal Structure in Early Glaucoma.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To investigate the correlations between retinal structure parameters and chromatic sensitivity in controls and people with various stages of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and ocular hypertension (OHT). A secondary aim was to assess the diagnostic and predictive accuracy of red/green (RG) and yellow/blue (YB) chromatic thresholds in identifying early glaucomatous alterations.
METHODS: One hundred sixty-nine participants were recruited (n = 25 OHT, n = 33 early, n = 11 moderate, n = 11 severe POAG, and n = 89 controls) from the glaucoma clinic at St. Thomas's Hospital. Chromatic sensitivity was measured with the Color Assessment and Diagnostics (CAD) test. Macular retinal layers and peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thicknesses (pRNFLT) were measured using OCT.
RESULTS: Median pRNFLT was significantly reduced in people with glaucoma of all stages compared to age-matched controls and OHT (P < 0.001). Significant negative correlations were found between RG thresholds and whole retinal thickness, ganglion cell layer (GCL), inner plexiform layer, inner and outer retinal layers and retinal pigment epithelium thickness in controls and glaucoma subgroups, whereas YB thresholds were correlated with GCL, outer retinal layer thickness and pRNFLT. Early POAG patients showed increased color thresholds (median RG = 3.40, YB = 4.04 CAD units) when compared to controls (RG = 1.86, YB = 2.20 CAD units) (P < 0.001). RG and YB thresholds showed considerable accuracy in detecting early POAG (area under the curves = 0.81 and 0.86, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Glaucoma patients show reduced chromatic sensitivity in every stage of severity. Results suggest that changes in both outer and inner retinal layers influence chromatic sensitivity. The outer retinal layer thickness is more strongly associated with color thresholds across all disease severity stages in glaucoma.

etudes.titre: Comparison of Outcomes of Anterior Chamber Intraocular Lenses with Scleral-fixated Intraocular Lenses: A Systematic Review.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: The absence of adequate posterior capsule support-whether due to complicated cataract surgery, lens subluxation due to trauma or syndromes, or aphakia due to any other cause-necessitates a suitable intraocular lens (IOL), either an anterior chamber intraocular lens (ACIOL) or a scleral-fixated IOL. The absence of any systematic review in the English literature comparing ACIOL with scleral-fixated IOL prompted this study. We looked for clinical trials (randomized and controlled) comparing the outcomes of ACIOL with scleral-fixated IOLs through various search engines. The searched terms included anterior chamber intraocular lens, scleral-fixated intraocular lens, complicated cataract surgery, and secondary intraocular lens. All patients who had either an ACIOL or scleral-fixated IOL were included. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Collaboration tools to ascertain the standard and quality of the trials. The outcomes studied were best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and intraoperative and postoperative complications. Seven trials were finally selected for analysis. There was no difference in BCVA between ACIOL and scleral-fixated IOL. There was also no difference in terms of complications, including retinal detachment, cystoid macular edema, glaucoma, uveitis, and vitreous prolapse, between the two groups. However, there was a higher chance of vitreous hemorrhage in the scleral-fixated group compared to ACIOL. Both ACIOL and scleral-fixated IOLs appear to be used as safe options in current practice. Further multicenter randomized controlled trials are needed to clarify the benefits of each intervention and strengthen the validity of this review.

etudes.titre: Unveiling the tumor: a rare case of choroidal melanoma concealed by emulsified silicone oil and retinal detachment.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume:
OBJECTIVE: To highlight the necessity of maintaining a high index of suspicion for the timely recognition and intervention in patients with choroidal melanoma and exudative retinal detachment masked by emulsified silicone oil.
METHODS: Case report.
RESULTS: We report a challenging case of a 61-year-old Hispanic male with a history of vitrectomy and silicone oil tamponade for presumed retinal detachment. The examination was notable for elevated intraocular pressure, anterior chamber emulsified silicone oil, and 360-degree posterior synechiae obscuring posterior segment visualization. Initial management targeted silicone oil-induced ocular hypertension, but persistent symptoms prompted surgical intervention. Intraoperatively, a large pigmented choroidal mass with associated exudative retinal detachment was discovered. Subsequent B-scan ultrasonography confirmed a dome-shaped choroidal tumor. Enucleation was performed, and histopathology confirmed choroidal melanoma with coexisting chronic pigmented perisilicone vitreoretinopathy.
CONCLUSION: This case highlights the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for intraocular tumors in patients with unexplained retinal detachments, especially when visualization is hindered by prior vitreoretinal surgery and emulsified silicone oil. Multimodal imaging, including ultrasonography or magnetic resonance imaging, should be considered in cases where clinical findings are incongruent or obscured. Timely recognition and intervention remain critical for optimal oncologic and visual outcomes.

etudes.titre: Uveitis and Interferon-Gamma Release Assay (IGRA) status: diagnostic implications of a positive IGRA test.
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « diagnostic »
etudes.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate and compare six-month clinical outcomes between uveitis patients with positive versus negative Interferon-Gamma Release Assay (IGRA) results, focusing on treatment success and complication rates.
METHODS: This prospective exploratory cohort study enrolled 54 adult patients with active uveitis at a tertiary eye care center. Participants were stratified into IGRA-positive and IGRA-negative groups based on baseline QuantiFERON test results. Patients received tailored treatment, including corticosteroids and anti-tubercular therapy (ATT) when indicated. Clinical follow-up occurred over a six-month period, and data were collected on visual acuity, ocular complications (e.g., glaucoma, cystoid macular edema), and overall treatment outcomes.
RESULTS: At baseline, IGRA-positive patients presented with more severe disease, including higher rates of visual impairment (43% vs. 27%) and blindness (9.5% vs. 3.0%). By six months, both groups had comparable treatment success rates. IGRA-positive patients experienced a lower rate of visual deterioration and showed clinical improvement despite their more severe baseline status. Although not statistically significant, IGRA-positive patients had higher incidences of glaucoma (9.5% vs. 3.0%) and cystoid macular edema (24% vs. 9.1%). Treatment failure was more frequent among patients with bilateral or intermediate uveitis, irrespective of IGRA status.
CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference in six-month outcomes was observed between the groups. Treatment success rate was noted to be lower in IGRA-positive patients although not statistically significant. Understanding the nuances of treatment success rate in uveitis patients, alongside stricter adherence monitoring and clear relapse management plans, could improve outcomes and provide a foundation for developing standardized treatment protocols in the future.
etudes.revue: Journal of ophthalmic inflammation and infection

etudes.titre: Primary Congenital Glaucoma in Kano, Northern Nigeria
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Background: Primary congenital glaucoma is one of the causes of childhood blindness and it appears to be common in our environment. This study evaluated the pattern of presentation and management of primary congenital glaucoma in children. Patients and Methods: This was a prospective questionnaire-based study of primary congenital glaucoma over a three year period. The information analyzed included patients' bio-data, vision, laterality of disease, presenting symptoms, family history, and history of traditional medicine application to the eye. Others included horizontal corneal diameter, intra ocular pressure and outcome of management. Results: There were 26 patients, 20 were males and 6 were females (M:F=3.3:1). Their ages ranged between 3 months and 5 years. Over a half of the patients presented during the first year of life. Primary congenital glaucoma was bilateral in 19 patients (73%). The commonest presenting symptoms were large eyes (85%), cloudy eyes (77%), photophobia (46%) and lacrimation (31%). In 44 eyes (98%) the intra ocular pressure was 20-49 mmHg before surgery and below 20 mmHg after surgery. Ttrabeculectomy resolved almost all the presenting symptoms, reduced intra-ocular pressure (IOP) and improved vision in all the patients. No sight threatening complications were recorded. Conclusion: Primary congenital glaucoma is common in our environment. Trabeculectomy remains a valuable treatment modality because it abolished most of the symptoms and IOP.

etudes.titre: Differences in corneal biomechanical parameters in normal tension glaucoma versus normotensive glaucoma suspect eyes
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « biomechanical »
etudes.resume: Abstract Multicenter retrospective study to evaluate differences in corneal biomechanical parameters provided by Corvis ST to segregate those with normal tension glaucoma (NTG) from glaucoma suspects. We included only newly diagnosed and treatment naïve glaucoma patients. Several corneal biomechanical parameters provided by Corvis ST were investigated. The discrimination ability of BGF was investigated through the area under the receiver operating characteristics curve (AUC). We included a total of 200 eyes from 100 patients with NTG and 200 eyes from 100 controls. We found statistical difference in Corneal velocity at second applanation (A2) with − 0.264 ± 0.061 m/s (OD) and − 0.270 ± 0.067 m/s (OS) in the control group, versus − 0.226 ± 0.084 m/s (OD, p = 0.0004) and − 0.223 ± 0.079 m/s (OS, p = 0.0001) in the NTG group. In addition, we found statistical difference in biomechanical glaucoma factor (BGF) between groups, with 0.568 ± 0.239 (OD) and 0.560 ± 0.229 (OS) in the control group, versus 0.674 ± 0.212 (OD, p = 0.001) and 0.659 ± 0.231 (OS, p = 0.056) in the NTG group. The AUC value was 0.63 BGF for discriminating NTG eyes from normal eyes. Both BGF and corneal velocity at second applanation were statistically different between groups. Using BGF parameter from Corvis ST can improve diagnostic accuracy when dealing with NTG.

etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a major cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, primarily due to optic nerve damage caused by elevated intraocular pressure. Early detection is vital to prevent vision loss, emphasizing the need for accurate and efficient diagnostic methods. The proposed model enhances optic disc (OD) and optic cup (OC) segmentation, as well as glaucoma classification, by integrating transformer-based attention and the convolutional block attention module (CBAM) into a UNet architecture. To improve segmentation precision, we employ multiscale losses at different decoding stages, allowing the network to progressively refine predictions across multiple resolution levels. By accurately segmenting OD and OC, we extract critical features for glaucoma risk assessment, combining these metrics with encoder features to enhance classification performance. The experimental results show that our approach significantly surpasses the existing methods in terms of both segmentation accuracy and glaucoma prediction, offering a reliable tool for early glaucoma diagnosis. For glaucoma classification, our method outperformed traditional approaches on the RIM-ONE, REFUGE, and DRISHTI-GS1 datasets, with accuracies of 95.8%, 96%, and 92%, respectively, and was comparable to that of the CUHKMED team, the leading team in the REFUGE challenge, achieving an accuracy of 95.59% on the REFUGE dataset. This advancement in automated glaucoma detection through deep learning can enable timely intervention, ultimately helping preserve the vision of patients.

etudes.titre: Explainable AI for glaucoma detection and classification: a comprehensive review
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « AI »; mot du titre : « detection »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is a leading cause of irreversible blindness and often advances without symptoms. This PRISMA/PICOS–guided systematic review synthesizes 100 studies (to January 2025) on artificial intelligence (AI) for glaucoma detection, staging, and monitoring using color fundus photography (CFP), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and OCT angiography (OCTA). Roughly 45% of studies use CFP, 55–60% use OCT, and 10–15% use OCTA; about one quarter fuse multiple imaging types with clinical data. Across methods—convolutional neural networks, Transformers, and hybrid fusion—internal test results are strong, with several systems reporting specialist-level sensitivity and specificity. Translation to practice remains limited by small, single-center cohorts, device/domain shifts that reduce generalization, a lack of prospective trials, and explainability approaches that are misaligned with clinical reasoning. We recommend multi-center, multi-ethnic, multi-vendor benchmarks, rigorous external and prospective validation, clinically meaningful and standardized explainability, and cost- and workflow-aware deployment. Addressing these gaps could enable earlier detection, more personalized monitoring, and real-world impact in reducing preventable blindness. Within this review, we investigate key challenges revolving around the use of AI models for glaucoma imaging across different learning paradigms, improving model efficiency, and coupling them with complementary techniques and multimodal data (CFP, OCT, and OCTA). We hope this review can give a comprehensive picture of AI-based methods for glaucoma to readers in the field of medical image analysis.

etudes.titre: Pitx2-associated early-onset glaucoma alters corneal innervation and sensory function in a sex-specific manner
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Abstract Purpose Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma is characterized by anterior segment dysgenesis, ocular hypertension, and optic neuropathy. Its consequences for corneal sensory innervation remain poorly understood. We investigated whether this disease alters corneal nerve structure and sensory function in a sex-dependent manner. Methods Male and female Pitx2 egl1/egl1 and Pitx2 +/+ mice were examined at 1 and 3 months. Ocular phenotyping included intraocular pressure, fundus imaging, visual evoked potentials, and optic nerve ultrastructure. RNA sequencing of corneas and trigeminal ganglia was performed at 3 months. Corneal innervation was assessed by βIII-tubulin immunofluorescence and volumetric quantification of nerve fibers. Corneal sensitivity was measured using Von Frey filaments. Results Pitx2 egl1/egl1 mice developed progressive ocular hypertension, fundus abnormalities, reduced visual evoked potential amplitudes, and optic nerve degeneration, supporting the model as early-onset glaucoma. Baseline sex-related transcriptional differences were limited in both cornea and trigeminal ganglia. In contrast, Pitx2 mutation induced sex-dependent molecular responses. Female corneas showed broader transcriptional changes enriched in inflammatory, stress-response, and tissue-remodeling pathways, whereas male corneas showed a more restricted response involving metabolic and homeostatic processes. Similar sex divergence was observed in trigeminal ganglia. Corneal nerve fiber volume was reduced in both sexes at 3 months but not at 1 month, whereas reduced sensitivity was detected only in mutant males. Conclusions This study identifies sexual dimorphism as a component of Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma. Furthermore, our findings suggest that glaucoma affects the corneal sensory system beyond optic nerve pathology, highlighting a potentially overlooked dimension of disease relevant to ocular surface monitoring and patient management. Highlights Disruption of the cornea–trigeminal ganglion axis with coordinated molecular and functional alterations in Pitx2-associated early-onset glaucoma Sex-dependent modifications in both cornea and trigeminal ganglion responses to early-onset glaucoma Progressive corneal neurodegeneration in early-onset glaucoma

etudes.titre: Mechanisms of Neurodegeneration and Retinal Imaging Biomarkers in Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Imaging »; mot du titre : « Biomarkers »
etudes.resume: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide and is characterized by progressive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) neurodegeneration with optic nerve head (ONH) damage and visual field loss. Although intraocular pressure (IOP) is the main modifiable risk factor, disease onset and progression reflect a multifactorial cascade involving mechanical strain at the lamina cribrosa, impaired axonal transport, neurovascular dysregulation with early neurovascular unit dysfunction, oxidative stress, mitochondrial failure, and chronic glial-driven neuroinflammation. Alongside IOP lowering, neuroprotective strategies have gained increasing attention; among the most studied, citicoline, nicotinamide, and coenzyme Q10 are supported by a strong biological rationale and encouraging early clinical signals, although robust evidence for long-term clinical efficacy remains limited. Because functional defects typically emerge only after substantial RGC loss, structural biomarkers are pivotal for early detection and monitoring. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides high-resolution, quantitative assessment of circumpapillary RNFL thickness, macular ganglion cell-related metrics, and ONH rim measures such as Bruch’s membrane opening-minimum rim width. OCT angiography (OCTA) complements OCT by quantifying retinal and peripapillary microvascular abnormalities, although its temporal and clinical relationship with neural loss remains incompletely defined. Longitudinal OCT follow-up can be supported by event-based and trend-based analyses to distinguish true change from test-retest variability and estimate rates of structural loss. Detection of Apoptosing Retinal Cells (DARC) represents an emerging investigational approach for in vivo visualization of retinal cell apoptosis. Overall, these advances support a multimodal structure-function-biomarker framework for glaucoma assessment while highlighting important clinical gaps that remain to be addressed.

etudes.titre: Essential Vascular Supply of the Eye in Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: This project is a comprehensive review of the vascular supply of the eye, tracing a continuous pathway from the heart and aortic arch through the great vessels, carotid system, circle of Willis, and ophthalmic artery to the intraocular microvasculature, including its venous and lymphatic drainage. Each vascular segment is examined for its normal anatomy and clinically relevant variation, its pathophysiology, and the congenital, acute, and chronic diseases specific to it, read throughout through the lens of ocular perfusion and its relationship to glaucoma. Elevated intraocular pressure remains the only proven modifiable risk factor for glaucoma, yet many patients progress despite adequate pressure control, and a vascular contribution to glaucomatous optic neuropathy has long been proposed. This review addresses the absence of a single work that treats the ocular vascular supply as one continuous system tied to that contribution. The review draws on a PRISMA-guided literature search across PubMed, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Google Scholar, and ProQuest. It builds directly on existing anatomical reviews of ocular vasculature and the established literature on ocular perfusion pressure in glaucoma. Its contribution is the integration of a continuous systemic-to-ocular pathway with a consistent disease framework applied to every segment. Expected outcomes are a peer-reviewed manuscript targeted for submission, multiple figures detailing blood perfusion, and a table mapping each vascular segment to its variation, associated disease, and ocular or glaucoma-related consequence.

etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Visual Field »
etudes.resume: Abstract Importance Artificial intelligence (AI) is under active development to support diagnosis and prognostication of glaucoma from visual fields (VF). These systems do not audit for vertical- meridian-respecting field loss patterns—known sequelae of stroke, hemorrhage, and neoplasm. Objective To develop a self-supervised encoder of automated perimetry that learns anatomically interpretable visual field structure without labels and to evaluate its capacity to identify suspected neurologic VF patterns in an independent public glaucoma dataset. Design, Setting, and Participants Diagnostic study (TRIPOD+AI). Pretraining: 23,223 unlabeled Humphrey VFs (patient-grouped training split of 28,943 fields from 3,871 University of Washington patients; UWHVF, all-comers perimetry). External evaluation: Harvard-Glaucoma Fairness dataset (Harvard-GF; 3,300 patients with paired VF and OCT from a single academic center). The encoder was never exposed to Harvard-GF during training. Exposures A 128-dimensional masked autoencoder of monocular Humphrey VF pattern- deviation data, with a supervised linear classifier on vertical-midline latent dimensions trained on per-eye expert neurological/nonneurological labels. Main Outcomes and Measures Primary: classifier accuracy under hard-negative evaluation (cross-validated balanced accuracy and AUC). Secondary: held-out specificity on structurally separated UWHVF controls; expert confirmation and OCT structural correlates of classifier- identified Harvard-GF suspects. Results Masked reconstruction recovered structure concordant with retinal neuroanatomy; 50 of 128 latent dimensions emerged spatially specialized (vs 23 for the TD encoder). Under hard- negative evaluation the classifier achieved cross-validated balanced accuracy 0.78 (95% CI, 0.75-0.82) and AUC 0.85 (95% CI, 0.82-0.89), with no false positives among 100 held-out controls. Applied to Harvard-GF without fine-tuning, it identified a top-20 of 1,748 glaucoma- labeled patients (1.1%) with morphology inconsistent with glaucoma; all 20 were NHT-positive (mean 62.4), and OCT showed preserved superior (Cohen d = +0.68; P < .001) and inferior (d = +0.63; P = .003) RNFL versus severity-matched controls. Conclusions and Relevance A self-supervised VF encoder learned anatomically interpretable visual field structure from unlabeled data and identified suspected neurological cases in a curated glaucoma dataset, with expert, rule-based, and OCT corroboration. Visual field datasets used to train glaucoma AI may benefit from neurological screening; the encoder reported here supports such audits and provides a foundation for neuro-ophthalmic AI beyond fundus photography and OCT. Key Points Question Can self-supervised learning learn anatomically interpretable visual field structure from unlabeled visual fields and identify neurological field loss? Findings Trained on 28,943 unlabeled visual fields, the encoder learned anatomically interpretable visual field structure and revealed ≥20 of 1,748 patients (≥1.1%) in an external glaucoma dataset with vertical-midline loss and retinal nerve fiber layer preservation. Meaning A self-supervised encoder learned anatomically interpretable visual field structure, and can audit glaucoma datasets for neurological field loss, reducing the risk that future AI misclassifies intracranial disease.

etudes.titre: A Gamified Virtual Reality Perimeter for Rapid Glaucoma Pre-Screening in Community Settings: Pilot Evaluation of "Meteor Blaster VR" (Preprint)
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Screening »
etudes.resume: BACKGROUND Undiagnosed glaucoma remains highly prevalent, and raising awareness of subtle visual impairments in daily life is essential for early detection. Although virtual reality (VR)–based perimetry has previously been investigated, little is known about whether a gamified VR system can accurately detect glaucomatous visual field loss while maintaining user engagement, which could enable opportunistic pre-screening for glaucoma. Therefore, we developed an immersive VR shooting game, Meteor Blaster VR. OBJECTIVE The study included 23 eyes of 23 patients with glaucoma and 28 eyes of 28 patients without glaucoma. To avoid the correlation between paired eyes, only right eyes were included in the analysis. Associations between game score and HFA indices were evaluated, and the diagnostic performance for glaucoma was assessed using receiver operating characteristics curves. METHODS The study included 23 eyes of 23 patients with glaucoma and 28 eyes of 28 patients without glaucoma. To avoid the correlation between paired eyes, only right eyes were included in the analysis. Associations between game score and HFA indices were evaluated, and the diagnostic performance for glaucoma was assessed using receiver operating characteristics curves. RESULTS There was no significant difference in age between the glaucoma group and the non-glaucoma group (54.7 ± 7.2 years vs. 58.0 ± 11.2 years, respectively; P = 0.234). On the other hand, there was a significant difference in game score (glaucoma 24.2 ± 5.3 vs. non-glaucoma 29.1 ± 2.4; P = 0.005). There was a significant correlation between game score and mean deviation (MD): for the entire visual field, the Pearson correlation coefficient was r = 0.85 (P < 0.001); for the upper half, r = 0.88 (P < 0.001); and for the lower half, r = 0.73 (P < 0.001). MD was the only independent predictor of game score (β = 0.90, adjusted R² = 0.72). Logistic regression analysis for game score showed relatively good glaucoma diagnostic performance (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.81, P < 0.001), and combining age with game score improved glaucoma discrimination ability (AUC = 0.83, P < 0.001). In contrast, age alone did not provide sufficient discriminatory ability for glaucoma (AUC = 0.65, P = 0.222). CONCLUSIONS The gamified VR platform demonstrated strong agreement with conventional visual field indices and may serve as an accessible, low-barrier pre-screening tool to prompt players to be aware of their visual status, thereby facilitating early glaucoma detection in an everyday community setting.

etudes.titre: Effect of iStent inject on unmedicated intraocular pressure in glaucoma: exploratory analysis of clinical trial data
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « iStent »
etudes.resume: Abstract Purpose The direct effect of iStent inject on intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with glaucoma is difficult to quantify in pragmatic trials where rates of post-surgical IOP-lowering therapy differ between intervention groups. We aimed to quantify the causal effect of iStent inject on unmedicated IOP at 12- and 24-months post-surgery. Methods Adults with mild-to-moderate glaucoma were 1:1 randomised to receive cataract surgery with iStent inject or cataract surgery alone at an Australian hospital (2017-2020, NCT03106181 ). IOP-lowering medications were prescribed as per clinician discretion. An exploratory analysis was used to estimate the controlled direct effect of iStent inject on IOP, analogous to the effect expected if all participants had undergone medication washout prior to assessment. Results Ninety-five eyes from 80 people were included (67.4% male, mean age 73.0 years, mean baseline IOP 17.1 mmHg). IOP-lowering medication was required for 53% of eyes in each group at 12 months (n=76); at 24 months (n=86) it was required for 43% and 64% in the active and control groups, respectively. Mean IOP was similar between intervention groups at each outcome visit. The controlled direct effect favoured the iStent inject group at 12 months (-2.1-mmHg difference, 95% CI -4.0,-0.3) but was attenuated at 24 months (-0.5 mmHg-difference, 95% CI -2.6,1.6). Conclusion Although the iStent inject was estimated to have an effect on lowering unmedicated IOP at 12 months, this effect had largely disappeared by 24 months. Medication washout is recommended when safe and practical in future trials to estimate these direct effects with more certainty.

etudes.titre: Enantiomorphic Glaucoma Displayed in Monozygotic Twins
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Background: Numerous theories exist about the etiology of glaucoma and various forms of research, including twin studies, are conducted to provide answers. Twin studies are an exceptional method of examining the genetic and environmental influences on primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) since comparison of monozygotic and dizygotic twins can infer a genetic causative factor. Case Report: A pair of monozygotic twins revealed strikingly similar examination results with the eventual diagnosis of POAG. Visual fields and fundus photography revealed enantiomorphic, or mirror image, likeness. The right eye of twin one (T1) and the left eye of twin two (T2) displayed a repeatable inferior arcuate defect and retinal nerve fiber layer defects (RNFL). Conclusion: An obvious genetic link within POAG is demonstrated by these twins. A dual case presentation will be described and a conclusion of the genetic backbone of glaucoma will be presented with supporting research. These studies provide information on genes responsible for POAG, environmental factors inducing POAG, and more insight for clinicians and patients so that better treatments may evolve in the future.

etudes.titre: Primary intraocular lens implantation is associated with lower observed odds of secondary glaucoma than aphakia after congenital cataract surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « surgery »
etudes.resume: This registration documents a systematic review and meta-analysis that synthesizes the comparative evidence on the risk of secondary glaucoma after primary intraocular lens (IOL) implantation versus aphakia in children undergoing surgery for congenital or infantile cataract. Purpose. Secondary glaucoma is a major sight-threatening complication of congenital/infantile cataract extraction, and the choice of optical rehabilitation—primary IOL implantation or correction of aphakia—may influence long-term glaucoma risk. Existing evidence is conflicting and the evidence base has expanded substantially since earlier comparative syntheses, motivating an updated comparison restricted to studies that contain both lens-status groups and report glaucoma outcomes separately. The primary aim is to compare the within-study odds of secondary glaucoma after primary IOL implantation relative to aphakia; secondary aims are to examine whether any association varies by study design (retrospective versus prospective/randomized), age at surgery, geographic region, and mean follow-up duration, and to estimate single-arm pooled incidence of secondary glaucoma in each group. Methods. The review was conducted and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Google Scholar, the Cochrane Library, and CNKI were searched from January 1999 through August 8, 2026, using search strings that combined concepts for cataract surgery/lensectomy, congenital/infantile/pediatric cataract, glaucoma, intraocular lens/pseudophakia, and aphakia; reference lists of included studies and prior reviews were also screened. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials and prospective or retrospective comparative cohorts of children undergoing cataract extraction for congenital or infantile cataract, with primary IOL implantation as the intervention and aphakia as the comparator, and with glaucoma outcomes reported separately for both groups. Studies of traumatic, drug-induced, metabolic, or secondary cataract, pre-existing congenital glaucoma, non-separable severe ocular anomalies, and follow-up shorter than one year were excluded. Records were screened independently in two stages (title/abstract and full text) by two investigators, and disagreements were resolved by discussion and consensus; data were extracted independently in duplicate using a standardized form. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool for randomized trials and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for observational studies. Study-specific odds ratios were pooled with random-effects inverse-variance meta-analysis using restricted maximum likelihood estimation and the Hartung-Knapp adjustment; heterogeneity was quantified, and prespecified subgroup, sensitivity, influence, and small-study-effect analyses were planned, with certainty of evidence assessed using the GRADE approach. Expected outcomes. The review was designed to deliver (1) a pooled within-study odds ratio with 95% confidence and prediction intervals for secondary glaucoma in the primary IOL group versus the aphakia group, (2) subgroup estimates by study design, age at surgery, geographic region, and follow-up duration, (3) single-arm pooled incidence of secondary glaucoma in each group, (4) measures of between-study heterogeneity together with an assessment of small-study effects and robustness, and (5) a GRADE-based rating of the certainty of evidence, with implications for surgical decision-making and recommendations for future research. As a retrospective registration, this record documents the methods of the completed review.

etudes.titre: Accessibility of Open-Angle Glaucoma Patient Education Materials Written and Simplified by AI Chatbots (Preprint)
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « AI »
etudes.resume: BACKGROUND Through handouts, physicians can offer patient information that lasts outside of appointments. However, patient education materials (PEMs) must be accessible to a patient audience, including being written at a suitable reading grade level. Organizations like the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) have improved accessibility of high-quality online resources, particularly within the field of glaucoma. However, topics are limited and readability of PEMs varies depending on disease process. OBJECTIVE Readability of glaucoma patient education materials (PEMs) generated by ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and OpenEvidence was compared to American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) and UpToDate resources to determine whether these large language models (LLMs) adjust reading levels to a fifth-grade standard. METHODS Three freely available LLMs—ChatGPT (GPT-5.1), Google Gemini (Flash 2.5), and OpenEvidence (2.0)—were used to generate glaucoma PEMs. Readability was scored before and after a standardized language simplification prompt using Flesch Reading Ease (FRE) and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL). Readability was compared across LLMs and against AAO and UpToDate patient materials using paired t-tests and ANOVA with Bonferroni correction. RESULTS LLM-generated PEMs exceeded a fifth-grade level as measured by FKGL (all p ≤ 0.03). Following prompting for language simplification, the LLMs significantly reduced reading grade level (all p < 0.05) and achieved FKGL near the fifth-grade (all p < 0.05), with Google Gemini producing the highest FRE and lowest FKGL. Simplified LLM-generated PEMs were significantly more readable than AAO materials (all p ≤ 0.02) and comparable to UpToDate patient education articles, which were already written around a sixth-grade reading level. CONCLUSIONS LLM-based AI tools can be prompted to generate glaucoma PEMs with readability approaching recommended fifth-grade levels. While unprompted outputs remain too complex, targeted language simplification substantially improves accessibility.

etudes.titre: Efeitos Vasculares no Glaucoma de Pressão Normal
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: O glaucoma de pressão normal representa uma variante clínica complexa do glaucoma primário de ângulo aberto, caracterizada pelo desenvolvimento de neuropatia óptica típica e perda progressiva de campo visual, mesmo com a pressão intraocular mantendo-se constantemente em níveis estatisticamente normais, ou seja, menores ou iguais a vinte e um milímetros de mercúrio. Tradicionalmente, o manejo do glaucoma concentrava-se de forma quase exclusiva nos fatores mecânicos pressóricos, porém a persistência da progressão do dano axonal em uma parcela significativa de pacientes com pressão controlada direcionou a atenção da comunidade científica para mecanismos alternativos de lesão celular. Diante desse cenário patogênico multifatorial, o presente estudo tem como objetivo realizar uma revisão sistemática da literatura para analisar os efeitos vasculares no glaucoma de pressão normal, discutindo as principais alterações na perfusão ocular, a regulação do fluxo sanguíneo e suas implicações clínicas na população brasileira. Para tanto, foi conduzido um levantamento bibliográfico nas bases de dados SciELO e LILACS utilizando descritores de saúde específicos para selecionar artigos de alta relevância científica no país. Os resultados evidenciam que a desregulação vascular primária, episódios frequentes de hipotensão arterial noturna e o fenômeno de vasoespasmo exercem um papel preponderante na indução de crises de isquemia e reperfusão na cabeça do nervo óptico. Conclui-se que o glaucoma de pressão normal deve ser compreendido como uma manifestação ocular de um distúrbio circulatório sistêmico, tornando indispensável a avaliação do perfil hemodinâmico global do paciente para instituir terapias neuroprotetoras e vasculares complementares eficazes.

etudes.titre: Mecanismos de Depósito Proteico no Glaucoma Pseudoesfoliativo
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: O glaucoma pseudoexfoliativo representa uma forma agressiva e complexa de glaucoma secundário de ângulo aberto, decorrente da síndrome de pseudoexfoliação, uma desordem generalizada da matriz extracelular relacionada ao envelhecimento. Esta condição clínica é caracterizada pela produção excessiva e pelo acúmulo progressivo de um material fibrilar esbranquiçado e amorfo em diversas estruturas do segmento anterior do olho, com especial tropismo pela cápsula anterior do cristalino, pela margem pupilar e pela malha trabecular. Diante do impacto severo que essa deposição exerce na dinâmica do humor aquoso e na integridade das estruturas oculares, o presente estudo tem como objetivo realizar uma revisão sistemática da literatura para analisar os mecanismos moleculares e bioquímicos envolvidos no depósito proteico do glaucoma pseudoexfoliativo, discutindo suas implicações na elevação da pressão intraocular e no manejo clínico dentro da realidade médica brasileira. Para isso, foi conduzida uma busca detalhada nas bases de dados SciELO e LILACS utilizando descritores em saúde controlados para selecionar artigos científicos de alta relevância nacional. Os resultados revelam que o estresse oxidativo crônico e a regulação positiva do fator de crescimento transformador beta um funcionam como os principais gatilhos para a síntese celular aberrante de glicoproteínas e proteoglicanos, cujo acúmulo na via de escoamento gera obstrução mecânica e disfunção endotelial trabecular. Conclui-se que o entendimento aprofundado desses caminhos bioquímicos é fundamental para otimizar as abordagens preventivas, antecipar complicações cirúrgicas decorrentes de fragilidade zonular e guiar terapias hipotensoras mais eficazes para conter o dano axonal crônico.

etudes.titre: Glaucoma: The Silent Thief of Sight as the End-Stage of the Brain's Ocular Decree
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Background: Glaucoma is currently defined as a progressive optic neuropathy characterised by retinal ganglion cell death and visual field loss, with elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) as the primary modifiable risk factor. Yet many patients continue to lose vision despite well-controlled IOP, and some develop glaucoma without ever having elevated pressure. This manuscript proposes that glaucoma is not primarily a pressure disease but the end-stage of the brain's ocular vasoconstrictive decree, executed over decades through chronic retinal and optic nerve head hypoxia. Framework: The brain's primary function is the maintenance of temperature and blood pH through the control of blood flow. Under chronic, unresolvable threat, the brain becomes a miser for blood. It constricts the choroid, retinal arterioles, and posterior ciliary arteries, producing the Stasis-Acidosis-Proteinopathy (SAP) cascade in the inner retina and optic nerve head. Retinal ganglion cells—among the most metabolically demanding neurons in the body—are starved. The amacrine network, especially the AII bridge, fails first functionally. Then the retinal ganglion cells die structurally. Intraocular pressure is an aggravating factor, not the root cause. Why Pressure-Lowering Alone Fails: Pressure-lowering drops suppress one mechanical blade. They do not restore choroidal or optic nerve perfusion. They do not resolve the brain's threat state. The Law of Pressure Reflection predicts that the hypoxic cascade continues despite normal IOP. This explains the clinical observation of progressive glaucoma in eyes with "controlled" pressure. Clinical Integration: The Ocular UBTI provides a non-invasive readout of the brain's ocular decree: choroidal thickness, retinal vessel calibre, OCTA perfusion density, RNFL thickness, and pupillary dynamics. The environmental path—quieting the knock, restoring sleep, reducing social threat—is primary. The starter motor (low-dose PDE5 inhibitor ± GLP-1 receptor agonist) is proposed as a time-limited vascular thaw for the starving optic nerve before irreversible cell death. Conclusion: Glaucoma is the silent thief because the brain steals blood from the optic nerve long before pressure rises. The eye appears normal until the retinal ganglion cells are already dying. The current model treats the thief's accomplice—pressure—while the real thief remains untouched. The framework redirects attention upstream, to the brain's decree and the hypoxic retina. Keywords: Glaucoma; retinal ganglion cells; optic nerve; hypoxia; choroid; vasoconstriction; SAP cascade; Ocular UBTI; intraocular pressure; Law of Pressure Reflection; environmental path; starter motor; PDE5 inhibitor; GLP-1

etudes.titre: Glaucoma and Diabetes Mellitus: A Comparative Evaluation of Comorbid Effect on Tear Quantity among Patients in Owerri, Imo State, Nigeria.
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Abstract Objective: Glaucoma is a chronic disorder that impairs ocular health and may exacerbate ocular surface disease leading to tear film instability, dry eye symptoms and decreased quality of life. This study compared changes in tear quantity among glaucoma subjects living with and without diabetes mellitus, attending an eye clinic in Nigeria. Methods: A comparative cross sectional research design was used. 157 subjects which comprised 74 glaucoma subjects living with diabetes mellitus and 83 glaucoma subjects living without diabetes mellitus participated in the study. Tear quantity assessment included the Schirmer I test and tear meniscus height (TMH) measurement. Descriptive statistics, independent samples t-test and Chi-square test were used to examine the data at 0.05 level of significance. Results: Glaucoma subjects living with diabetes mellitus showed substantially decreased tear production (11.4 +/- 6.8 mm) compared with glaucoma subjects living without diabetes mellitus (19.6 +/- 9.6 mm; p < 0.001). Tear meniscus height in glaucoma subjects living with diabetes mellitus (0.8 +/- 0.3 mm) was significantly greater than in subjects living without diabetes mellitus (0.7 +/- 0.3 mm; p = 0.034). Conclusion: Diabetes mellitus dramatically deteriorates the ocular surface function in glaucoma subjects by decreasing tear production, altering the tear meniscus height and increasing the severity of ocular surface symptoms. Routine glaucoma care, especially in patients with diabetes mellitus, should include a full ocular surface evaluation including Schirmer I test, TBUT, TMH, and OSDI assessment to allow early detection and management of ocular surface disease, better treatment adherence, and improved visual outcomes. Keywords: Glaucoma, Diabetes Mellitus, Tear production, Tear Meniscus Height, Ocular Surface Disease.

etudes.titre: Assessment of Tear film Stability and Ocular Surface Disease Index among Glaucoma Subjects living with and without Diabetes Mellitus in Owerri, Imo State, Nigeria
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Abstract Objective The ocular surface is an integral unit of the visual system. Its smooth and wet surface which is maintained by the tear film, is the most important refractive interface of the visual system. This study compared ocular surface alterations among glaucoma subjects living with and without diabetes mellitus in a Owerri, Imo State, Nigeria Methods Subjects diagnosed of glaucoma living with and without diabetes mellitus were included in the study. Ocular surface assessment included the Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) questionnaire, and tear break-up time (TBUT). Descriptive statistics, independent samples t-test and Chi-square test were used to examine the data at 0.05 level of significance. Results Considerable shorter tear break-up time (11.3 ± 9.0s) was seen among glaucoma subjects living with diabetes mellitus than those living without diabetes mellitus (16.0 ± 10.6s; p = 0.003), demonstrating the higher tear film instability. This was similarly reflected by the mean OSDI score, which was considerably higher in glaucoma patients living with diabetes mellitus (40.0 ± 23.4) compared with those without diabetes mellitus (28.1 ± 21.8; p = 0.001) showing a larger ocular surface symptom load. However, although the frequency of severe OSDI symptoms was greater in glaucoma subjects living with diabetes mellitus, the relationship between diabetes status and OSDI severity categories was not statistically significant (χ 2 = 7.584, p = 0.055). Conclusion Diabetes mellitus significantly impacts the health of the ocular surface in glaucoma subjects. The combination of glaucoma and diabetes may result in more rapid tear film instability, increased ocular pain, and decreased quality of life and adherence to long-term glaucoma medication.

etudes.titre: The potential of antioxidants as glaucoma therapy
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « antioxidants »
etudes.resume: BACKGROUND: Glaucoma is a form of progressively worsening optic neuropathy evidenced by the loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), with consequent visual impairment. While an elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) and oxidative stress are cornerstones in the pathological study of glaucoma, there is growing evidence that antioxidant supplementation may enhance ocular blood flow, reduce IOP, protect mitochondrial function, and decrease neuroinflammation, thus serving as a possible adjunctive treatment for glaucoma.METHODS: A systematic search of the literature was performed with the databases PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Springer Link using the keywords “antioxidant,” “glaucoma,” and “ocular hypertension” for studies published from the years 2020 to 2024. There were 4797 articles in the beginning, so all but the most relevant 13 were selected based on criteria such as randomized control trials, original research design, and systematic reviews predominantly focused on the proposed topic.RESULTS: The selected studies showed that oxidative stress is a significant contributing factor in the reduced blood flow to eyes, and that certain antioxidants, for example, vitamins C and E, Coenzyme Q10, hesperidin, as well as some natural extracts significantly improved the perfusion as well as lowers the IOP whilst protecting the RGCs from oxidized and apoptotic damage. A number of trials reported marked improvements.CONCLUSIONS: The information analyzed proves that antioxidants may be helpful as part of caring for persons with glaucoma. Antioxidant supplementation could lead to improved ocular blood circulation and reduced IOP because of enhanced mitochondral activity, and less oxidative stress to RGCs and trabecular meshwork (TM). These findings, however, need to be substantiated by better clinical trials capable of determining their ideal values in regard to dosage and long-term benefits. Studies, however, suggest that incorporating antioxidants into glaucoma management strategies is likely to ameliorate progressive glaucomatous damage and enhance the patient’s quality of life.
etudes.revue: Gazzetta Medica Italiana Archivio per le Scienze Mediche

etudes.titre: Sequential Inflammatory and Pupillary-Block Ocular Hypertension in Streptococcus suis Endogenous Endophthalmitis: An Observational Analytic Case Study
etudes.raison_rubrique: aucune règle de rubrique ne s'applique
etudes.resume: Background: Streptococcus suis, a zoonosis acquired from pigs and raw pork, is a rare cause of endogenous endophthalmitis, and no quantitative account of the pressure complications of such an eye has been published. Objective: To characterize, in a single culture-proven case of Streptococcus suis endogenous endophthalmitis, the two mechanisms and the course of the raised intraocular pressure, and to derive the clinical implications for management. Methods: a structured analysis of one culture-proven case managed at a tertiary hospital in Bali, Indonesia, over 48 days. Acuity was converted to logMAR on four published scales, all 19 pressure readings were analysed with a repeatability model, and corticosteroid causation was scored with the Naranjo instrument. Results: a 46-year-old man who had eaten raw pork a week earlier presented with meningitis, reduced hearing and a left eye with light perception, hypopyon and vitritis. Cerebrospinal fluid and vitreous both grew S. suis. Pressure rose in two distinct episodes: an inflammatory one peaking at 29.0 mmHg on day 7, and a pupillary block from posterior synechiae with iris bombé peaking at 30.0 mmHg on day 16, which fell 11.0 mmHg after iridotomy with simultaneous reintroduction of timolol. Corticosteroid causation scored 3, a value largely fixed by the temporal sequence alone. Acuity improved by 0.70 logMAR overall, but the division of that gain across the vitrectomy reversed with the conversion scale: 0.40 before and 0.30 after by clinical convention against 0.10 and 0.60 with measured hand-movement values. The eye remained blind. Conclusion: raised pressure in such eyes is not one entity, the pupil must be examined before pressure-lowering therapy is escalated, and a logMAR change at this level of vision is uninterpretable unless its scale is stated.

etudes.titre: Shrinkage invalidates the Hosmer-Lemeshow test: goodness of fit for penalized logistic regression, with an application to glaucoma diagnosis
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « diagnosis »
etudes.resume: Clinical prediction models are increasingly fitted by penalized logistic regression, because collinearity or many candidate predictors makes maximum likelihood unstable or impossible. Calibration is then almost always assessed by a grouped goodness-of-fit test such as the Hosmer-Lemeshow test. We show that this combination is invalid. Under ridge regression the grouped standardized residuals acquire a non-centrality induced by shrinkage, so the reference distribution used in practice is wrong, and at the penalty that most improves the fitted probabilities the test rejects correctly specified models between 92 and 100 per cent of the time. We derive the corrected law and define the shrinkage-corrected Hosmer-Lemeshow test, which subtracts an estimate of that non-centrality, restoring the maximum likelihood reference exactly to first order, and is made valid by prepivoting at a power cost we measure. We also give the attenuation law governing what any such test can detect once the linear predictor must be estimated. In glaucoma diagnosis by confocal laser tomography, where the maximum likelihood estimate does not exist, the corrected test finds the evidence for misfit weaker by more than three orders of magnitude: the fitted risks are too flat rather than mis-ordered, so the model needs recalibration rather than rebuilding.

etudes.titre: Mitochondrial DNA Copy Number Is Associated With Visual Field Progression in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
etudes.raison_rubrique: mot du titre : « Visual Field »
etudes.resume: A bstract Purpose To investigate the association between mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) copy number (CN) and the rate of visual field progression in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma. Design Retrospective cohort study Participants 200 patients with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) with a mean of 11 years of longitudinal clinical data and DNA extracted from peripheral blood. Methods DNA extraction was performed on peripheral blood leukocytes collected from 200 POAG patients who had an average follow-up of 11 years. Mitochondrial CN was quantified by multiplex quantitative TaqMan PCR using custom primers and probes against cytochrome b and ß-2 microglobulin as measures of mitochondrial and nuclear genes, respectively. Univariable and multivariable linear regression models were used to evaluate the association between mtDNA CN and rates of visual field progression, quantified by the slope of standard automated perimetry (SAP) mean deviation (MD) over time. Main Outcome Measures Association of mtDNA CN with MD slope. Results Mean mtDNA CN was 107.6 copies per cell (interquartile range, 70.5–126.7). Higher ln(mtDNA CN) was associated with slower rates of MD loss in both univariable ( β = 0.29, p < 0.001) and multivariable analyses ( β = 0.25, p = 0.003). Higher peak IOP was independently associated with faster visual field progression in both analyses. A significant interaction was observed between mtDNA CN and peak IOP ( β = −0.054, p < 0.001), with the association between lower mtDNA CN and faster SAP progression being more pronounced at lower levels of peak IOP. Conclusion Lower mtDNA CN was associated with faster SAP progression, with the association being most pronounced at lower levels of peak IOP. These findings support mtDNA CN as a potential systemic biomarker of mitochondrial genomic reserve and susceptibility to visual field loss.
